title: Fine-scale slope: gaps wider than 0.3 km are partially filled with fabricated WSE, biasing the published near-bifurcation slope
description: _fine_regular_grid documents 'per pass, interpolate internal gaps up to this wide' (FINE_FILL_GAP_KM=0.3, i.e. gaps of <= 3 bins). But pandas Series.interpolate(limit=3, limit_area='inside') does NOT skip longer gaps — it partially fills the first 3 NaNs of EVERY internal gap, however long, with values lying on the straight chord spanning the whole gap. Those fabricated bins (bins the pass never imaged, valued as a km-scale chord) then enter the sliding Theil–Sen fit (_fine_slope_theilsen treats them as observations), so per-pass slopes at gap edges reflect the gap-spanning average gradient, not the local 0.5 km structure the tab claims to resolve. On the full local archive, 229 of 324 reach-pass series are affected; 3,993 fabricated bins vs 5,827 intended short-gap fills; 5.3% of valid cells inside the headline 1–5 km bifurcation window are fabricated (and each contaminates neighboring windows in the +/-0.25 km sweep). The identical code is in thesis_figures/core.py:270 (thesis Figure 9) and slope_finescale_prototype.py:128, so the thesis figure inherits the same bias.
failure_scenario: Ran the exact pipeline (same SQL, npix>=30 filter, xmax=34, 0.5 km Theil–Sen sweep, n>=3 core mask, median over 1–5 km) on batch_outputs/master_all_data_part_*.parquet, all passes. CURRENT behavior: Kanektok 251.7, Uyak 229.0, 'Kanektok advantage here' = +22.7 cm/km. With the fill restricted to gaps <= 3 bins as documented: Kanektok 250.3, Uyak 234.8, advantage = +15.6 cm/km. The Uyak slope moves ~6 cm/km and the headline advantage metric shown on the Fine-Scale Slope tab (and fed into the thesis narrative of the local slope advantage) shrinks by ~30% — the displayed number is an artifact of fabricated interpolated bins, not the documented method.
suggested_fix: After s.interpolate(limit=max_gap, limit_area='inside'), blank the fills belonging to NaN runs longer than max_gap (identify runs in the original series and set those positions back to NaN), or interpolate without limit and mask any filled value whose enclosing original gap exceeds max_gap. Apply the same fix to thesis_figures/core.py:270 and slope_finescale_prototype.py:128, and re-generate thesis Figure 9 and the tab's quoted near-bifurcation numbers.

title: Cache keys never capture the data version: url_version is a constant, so the documented cache-busting cannot fire
description: The comment at 569–571 says the connection cache key (url_version) 'invalidates when the data source changes', and compute_finescale_pass_matrix's docstring says 'url_version keys the cache to the deployed data version'. But url_version is always the module constant REMOTE_PARQUET_URL — it can only change via a code edit, which redeploys and clears all caches anyway. The project's documented data-swap workflow (MEMORY: 'stable filename — swap data without code changes' on GitHub Release v2.0-data) changes the bytes behind the SAME URL, busting nothing. Meanwhile load_detrend_frame (line 200), load_dem_profile (626), load_dem_points (647), load_reference_gradient (1064), load_refgrad_decomposition (1078) and load_metadata (1108) have no data-version key at all — their outputs depend entirely on the data behind _con (which is excluded from the key), bounded only by ttl=86400.
failure_scenario: Swap dashboard_data.parquet in the GitHub release (or, locally, re-run SWOT_Pull.py adding new partition files while the app is running): the DuckDB views read the new data immediately, so uncached queries (viz_df, stats_df, diff_query, slope_query) reflect the new archive, while every @st.cache_data loader above serves frames computed from the OLD data for up to 24 hours. Tabs then disagree: e.g. the Hydraulic Gradient reference values and the DEM profile show stale numbers next to fresh profile/difference charts, and load_metadata hides newly ingested pass dates from the welcome page for up to a day.
suggested_fix: Derive a real data-version token (e.g. HTTP ETag/Last-Modified of the release asset, or max(Pass_Date)+row count for local partitions) at connection time and pass it as a plain cache-key argument to every data-dependent @st.cache_data loader; or correct the comments/docstrings to state that ttl=86400 is the only staleness bound.

title: Ice-season warning renders only in the data-reload branch and vanishes on the next full rerun
description: The 'Ice season data included' st.warning (lines 1346–1355) sits inside the `if "viz_df" not in st.session_state or viz_sig != selection_sig:` reload branch (line 1334). On any subsequent full rerun with the same selection the cached else-branch runs and the warning is never emitted again, even though winter passes are still selected and every chart still shows ice-contaminated WSE.
failure_scenario: User selects a December pass on the welcome page and launches: the warning appears once. They then box-select points on the Gradient Profile (on_select='rerun') or move the Cross-Sections radius slider — both trigger a full rerun that takes the cached path — and the scientific caution about 0.5–2+ m ice-inflated WSE silently disappears while the ice data remains in every tab.
suggested_fix: Move the ice_selected check and st.warning outside the reload branch (it depends only on selected_pass_dates, which is available on every run).

title: Fine-scale n_passes and the reliability gate count passes that contributed no data
description: In compute_finescale_pass_matrix, passes with fewer than 5 grid bins are skipped (`if len(ix) < 5: continue`) but still occupy an all-NaN column in `mat` and are counted in `passes`/`n_passes`. The legend label '(N passes)', the near-bifurcation table's 'Passes' column, and the MIN_PASSES_RELIABLE=10 warning gate (line 2832) therefore overstate the number of passes actually supporting the profile.
failure_scenario: A selection of 10 passes where 3 imaged fewer than 5 usable 0.1 km bins passes the 'Too few passes' gate (min pass_counts = 10 >= 10) and the chart legend claims 10 passes, while only 7 columns of the matrix contain any slope values — the exact selection-artifact condition the warning exists to catch.
suggested_fix: Count n_passes (and drive the gate) from columns with at least one finite value, e.g. np.isfinite(mat).any(axis=0).sum().

title: Return-to-Homepage comment claims pass checkbox states are preserved, but Streamlit garbage-collects them
description: The comment at 1274–1277 says '(pass_{date} widget states are preserved so the checkboxes still reflect the last choice.)'. They are not: the pass_{d} keys are widget-bound checkbox keys that only render on the welcome page, and Streamlit deletes widget-keyed session state at the end of any run in which the widget is not rendered — which the code itself acknowledges at 1290–1294 (the reason confirmed_pass_dates exists). Since Return-to-Homepage also pops confirmed_pass_dates and pass_defaults_initialized remains set, the welcome page renders with every checkbox unchecked and no re-defaulting.
failure_scenario: User launches the dashboard with a custom pass selection, interacts (any second full rerun GCs the pass_ keys), clicks 'Return to Homepage': the 'Choose Specific Dates' expander shows 0 passes selected instead of the last choice, and 'Launch Dashboard' warns 'Please select at least one pass'. No wrong data is shown (the fallback protects the dashboard), but the comment documents behavior that does not exist and the welcome page loses the user's selection.
suggested_fix: Either restore checkbox state on the welcome page from confirmed_pass_dates before rendering the checklist (and only pop confirmed after restoring), or fix the comment.

title: Reach names are interpolated into SQL without quoting/escaping
description: rivers_sql = "'" + "','".join(selected_reaches) + "'" embeds Reach_Name values taken from the parquet (SELECT DISTINCT Reach_Name) directly into every WHERE clause with no escaping. Not user-controllable today (values are the two fixed reach constants, verified in the data: only Kanektok_River and Uyak_Creek), but any future dataset whose reach name contains an apostrophe (e.g. O'Malley_Creek) breaks every query built from where_clause, and the same where_clause string is a cache key, so the malformed SQL is also cached.
failure_scenario: A third reach named "St. Mary's_Slough" is ingested: render_dashboard's COUNT query throws a DuckDB parser error on every launch and the dashboard st.stop()s.
suggested_fix: Escape single quotes (r.replace("'", "''")) when building rivers_sql, or use DuckDB parameter binding for the reach list.

title: Stage-invariance correlation is computed but never shown (temporal tab)
description: In Chart 2 of the Temporal Results tab, r = float(np.corrcoef(d["wse_ref_m"], d["slope_cm_km"])[0, 1]) is computed per reach but never used — corr_txt only reports the median slope. The caption's claim that 'the bands are flat' (i.e. slope is stage-invariant) is exactly what r would quantify, so the supporting statistic was evidently intended to be displayed and silently is not.
failure_scenario: A reader of the tab (or a committee member) asks for the correlation backing the 'water level has almost no effect' claim; the page presents none, although the code computes it and then discards it on every render.
suggested_fix: Include r in corr_txt (e.g. 'usually about {med:.0f} cm/km, r = {r:+.2f}') or delete the computation.

title: Gap-fill interpolate(limit=3) fabricates WSE in long gaps instead of skipping them
description: _fine_regular_grid is documented as 'interpolate internal gaps up to this wide' (FINE_FILL_GAP_KM = 0.3 km = 3 bins), but pandas Series.interpolate(limit=3, limit_area='inside') does NOT restrict filling to gaps <= 3 bins: it fills the FIRST 3 NaNs of EVERY interior gap regardless of gap length (and only from the left, since limit_direction defaults to 'forward'). Those filled bins lie on the straight chord between the gap's endpoints, so the per-pass Theil-Sen slope near the upstream edge of every long coverage gap is the chord slope across the whole gap, not a measured local slope. The identical line exists in dashboard_swot.py:351, so both the Fine-Scale Slope tab and thesis Fig 9 (core.finescale_slope_profile) consume fabricated data.
failure_scenario: Demonstrated: pd.Series([1,nan*6,8]).interpolate(limit=3, limit_area='inside') -> [1,2,3,4,nan,nan,nan,8], i.e. 3 fabricated points inside a 6-bin gap. Reproducing the full pipeline on batch_outputs/master_all_data.parquet (open-water, 2025-04-17 excluded, res=0.5 km, xmax=34): 149 of 213 reach-passes contain interior gaps > 0.3 km, injecting 2,532 fabricated 100-m bins into the Theil-Sen fits. Versus a corrected fill (only gaps <= 3 bins), the aggregated median profile (min_passes=3, exactly Fig 9) changes at 211/338 Uyak bins by > 1 cm/km, worst-case 124 cm/km (Uyak at 5.0-5.2 km: 253 -> 326 cm/km at 5.0 km, which is inside the 1-5 km headline window edge); Kanektok worst-case 62 cm/km at 30.1 km. Per-pass 1-5 km window slopes ('Slope over time' view) shift up to 22 cm/km and the >=80%-coverage gated pass count changes (Uyak 42 -> 30). The headline medians are robust (Kanektok 258.9 -> 258.0; Uyak 1-5 km median unchanged; paired advantage moves ~1 cm/km), but the published Fig 9 profile curve is materially wrong at sparse-coverage locations.
suggested_fix: After the limited interpolate, mask back to NaN any filled values that belong to a NaN run longer than max_gap (compute run lengths on the pre-fill NaN mask), or fill via a run-length-aware routine. Apply identically in dashboard_swot.py:351 and core.py:270 to keep them in lockstep.

title: abs() of signed quantiles produces a band that can exclude the plotted median
description: finescale_slope_profile (and dashboard _fine_aggregate, dashboard_swot.py:446) computes q25/q75 of the SIGNED per-pass slopes, then plots steepness as lo=min(|q25|,|q75|), hi=max(|q25|,|q75|), med=|median|. When per-pass slopes straddle zero (q25 < 0 < q75), |quantile| is not a quantile of |slope|: both |q25| and |q75| can exceed |median|, so the plotted median falls BELOW the band's lower edge and the shaded 'IQR' is no longer a 25-75% interval of anything.
failure_scenario: Real data (full archive, exact Fig 9 pipeline): Uyak Creek bins at 33.5, 33.7, 33.9, 34.0 km (all with n >= 3, so plotted in Fig 9's full panel and the dashboard aggregate view) have plotted medians of 7.2, 8.6, 2.0, 12.8 cm/km sitting below band lower edges of 14.9, 8.8, 19.1, 14.0 cm/km; Kanektok has 2 such bins (33.9, 34.0 km). Synthetic: signed slopes [-2, +0.1, +1] -> q25=-0.95, q75=0.55, median=0.1; plotted band [0.55, 0.95] excludes plotted med 0.1.
suggested_fix: Where the signed IQR straddles zero, clamp lo to min(lo, med) (or 0), or plot signed slope with a sign-flip note; alternatively compute the band as quantiles of |slope| but keep med=|median(signed)| documented as such.

title: Slope Profile stats table swaps 'Slope at Coast' and 'Slope at Anchor'
description: calculate_slope_profile returns x_eval = linspace(min_dist, max_dist), so index 0 is the SMALLEST distance-from-anchor (the anchor end) and index -1 is the largest (~35-36 km, the coast/mouth). The stats table maps abs_slope[0] to 'Slope at Coast (cm/km)' and abs_slope[-1] to 'Slope at Anchor (cm/km)' (lines 2739-2740) — exactly backwards. The app's own convention is unambiguous: tab1's explainer says 'the coast/river mouth is on the left (~36 km); the anchor point is on the right (0 km)', and full-archive median WSE is 62.9 m at dist 0 vs 1.8 m at 35 km, so dist=0 is the inland anchor.
failure_scenario: Ran the exact calculate_slope_profile math on the full local archive: Kanektok x_eval[0]=0.30 km (anchor side) has |slope|=125.4 cm/km and is shown as 'Slope at Coast'; x_eval[-1]=35.10 km (the actual coast) has |slope|=41.5 cm/km and is shown as 'Slope at Anchor'. Uyak: 115.7 vs 43.6 identically swapped. Any user reading the table concludes the rivers are steep at the coast and gentle at the anchor — the opposite of reality (both rivers are steep near the anchor, gentle at the tidal mouth).
suggested_fix: Swap the two labels: 'Slope at Anchor (cm/km)': abs_slope[0], 'Slope at Coast (cm/km)': abs_slope[-1].

title: calculate_slope_profile smooths across missing 100-m bins as if adjacent
description: calculate_slope_profile (identical in thesis_figures/core.py:199) drops empty 100-m bins from bin_medians and then runs gaussian_filter1d(sigma=smooth_km/bin_size) on the COMPACTED array, so bins on opposite sides of an unobserved stretch are treated as 0.1 km apart. np.interp then linearly bridges the gap on the physical axis, and np.gradient reports a smooth, plausible-looking slope through river that was never observed, while also distorting slopes adjacent to the gap (the effective smoothing window in km shrinks across gaps).
failure_scenario: Synthetic demonstration: uniform true slope 200 cm/km with a 3 km unobserved gap (bins 100-129 missing) -> computed |slope| inside/near the gap is 1-32 cm/km, i.e. up to 99% low. Full-archive pooled data currently has ZERO missing interior bins for both rivers (verified), so thesis Fig 8 is unaffected -- but the dashboard runs this on arbitrary pass selections (line 2714 with the user's where_clause; line 1449 on the 15k-point viz_df sample), and partial-coverage passes exist (e.g. 2026-07-09 Kanektok images only 45 of ~350 bins), so a multi-pass selection with disjoint coverage produces confidently wrong slope curves over unobserved reaches.
suggested_fix: Reindex the binned medians onto the full regular grid with NaNs, smooth with a NaN-aware Gaussian (normalized convolution), and return NaN slope where local coverage is absent instead of interpolating across gaps.

title: Dashboard's LOESS detrending is index-space smoothing with density-dependent bandwidth
description: The 'LOESS' branch of calculate_detrending is gaussian_filter1d over y sorted by x with sigma = 0.15*N/3 SAMPLES, not a local regression in distance: the physical bandwidth varies inversely with local point density along the reach and with total N (so the same selection sampled at a different size yields a different baseline, and residual outlier flags shift). Identical code is in thesis_figures/core.py:150. Currently unreachable in practice -- the dashboard hardcodes detrend_method = 'Polynomial (2nd order)' (line 1320) and Fig 7 uses the polynomial -- but it remains a selectable-looking method name that misdescribes the estimator.
failure_scenario: Two selections with identical spatial support but different point counts (e.g. 30,000-point systematic sample vs full data) produce different LOESS baselines purely because sigma scales with N; residuals and Modified-Z outlier flags then differ. In a reach segment with 10x point density the effective smoothing window is 10x narrower in km, so the 'baseline' absorbs real local structure there while over-smoothing sparse segments.
suggested_fix: Either remove the branch (it is dead with the hardcoded method) or implement distance-domain smoothing (e.g. fixed-km Gaussian on binned medians, as elsewhere in the codebase) and rename it honestly.

title: np.round (half-to-even) vs DuckDB ROUND (half-away) bin points on .5 boundaries differently
description: The pipeline mixes three rounding conventions for the same 0.1-km binning: numpy np.round in calculate_slope_profile (line 257; banker's rounding: round(2.5)=2), DuckDB ROUND in compute_finescale_pass_matrix (line 387; half-away-from-zero: ROUND(2.5)=3), and pandas Series.round in core.elevation_difference (core.py:378) and Fig 7's node binning (banker's). Verified: for x=0.25, np.round(x/0.1)=2 while DuckDB ROUND(x/0.1)=3, so the same point lands in different bins depending on code path.
failure_scenario: Ran both against the archive: 24 real points in master_all_data.parquet fall exactly on a .5 boundary of the 0.1-km binning and are assigned to different bins by the numpy/pandas paths vs the DuckDB path. With 7.9M points the effect on any median is negligible today, but figures that juxtapose the two paths (fine-scale slope vs elevation-difference/slope-profile) are not bit-reproducible against each other at bin boundaries, and the discrepancy grows if binning is ever applied to already-quantized distances.
suggested_fix: Standardize on FLOOR(dist_km/bin)+0.5*bin (half-open bins) or a single rounding convention implemented in one shared helper used by both SQL and Python paths.

title: compute_finescale_slope is dead code and silently diverges from core's gating
description: compute_finescale_slope is never called anywhere in dashboard_swot.py (the Fine-Scale tab uses compute_finescale_pass_matrix + _fine_aggregate directly and applies its own n>=3 display gate). It also aggregates with _fine_aggregate's default min_passes=0, whereas the 'verbatim' counterpart thesis_figures/core.py:finescale_slope_profile defaults min_passes=3 -- so if this wrapper were ever used, its output would include 1-2-pass bins that Fig 9 masks, violating the module's 'keep them in lockstep' contract.
failure_scenario: A future caller uses compute_finescale_slope expecting the tab/Fig-9 behavior: bins imaged by only 1-2 passes return a 'median' equal to that single pass's slope with a zero-width band, instead of NaN. On the full archive this affects the sparse-coverage bins where n < 3 (present at reach edges and gap regions).
suggested_fix: Delete the wrapper, or make it call _fine_aggregate(r['mat'], min_passes=3) and actually use it in the tab.

title: calculate_detrending crashes or warns on degenerate (<3 point) inputs
description: load_detrend_frame only guards len(bdf)==0 before calling calculate_detrending. stats.linregress raises ValueError for a single point and returns NaN slope for 2 identical-x points; np.polynomial.Polynomial.fit with fewer points than degree+1 raises or produces a rank-deficient warning with an unstable baseline. The same applies to thesis core.calculate_detrending (core.py:126).
failure_scenario: A dashboard selection whose where_clause matches exactly 1 row (a single pass clipped to a tiny reach subset -- achievable via the pass/reach filters) reaches calculate_detrending with n=1: scipy raises ValueError('Inputs must not be empty' / needs 2 points), which surfaces as an uncaught exception in the Detrended Profile tab instead of the existing friendly 'No data available' warning.
suggested_fix: Extend the guard to require a minimum point count (e.g. n >= 10, matching the slope tab's existing threshold) before fitting, returning the empty-data path otherwise.

title: Fine-scale IQR band from abs() of signed quantiles is wrong where slopes straddle zero; median line plots outside its own band
description: _fine_aggregate computes signed q25/q75 across passes, then derives the plotted band as [min(|q25|,|q75|), max(|q25|,|q75|)] and the line as |median| (lines 444-446). When per-pass slopes straddle zero (flat/tidal downstream bins), this is not the IQR of |slope|: the band excludes zero, misses the true absolute-slope quartiles, and can exclude the plotted median itself.
failure_scenario: Reproduced the full compute_finescale_pass_matrix + _fine_aggregate pipeline on the local archive (all passes). 12 displayed core bins (n>=3) have q25<0<q75, and in 7 of them the plotted median lies OUTSIDE the plotted band — e.g. Uyak 33.6 km: plotted median 6.5 cm/km with band [16.4, 36.8], while the correct |slope| stats are median 27.2, IQR [13.1, 48.9]; Kanektok 33.9 km: plotted median 6.8 with band [42.0, 44.5], correct median 44.1, IQR [17.6, 93.5]. Affected bins are at 29.9 km and 33.3-34.0 km, inside the 34 km display cut, so the Aggregate-profile view draws a visibly broken line-outside-band there. The 1-5 km near-bifurcation headline numbers are NOT affected (slopes there are far from zero).
suggested_fix: Take abs first, then aggregate: med/q25/q75 of np.abs(sub) (or plot signed slopes with a signed band). Same issue applies in spirit to np.abs(nanmedian(...)) in _fine_window_slope, though the 1-5 km window never straddles zero in practice.

title: Temporal tab 'Lower river (<=18 km)' / 'Upper river (>18 km)' labels are geographically inverted
description: The Q3 typhoon table maps downstream_dwse_m (computed over dist_km <= 18) to 'Lower river (<=18 km)' and upstream_dwse_m (dist_km > 18) to 'Upper river (>18 km)'. But dist_km is distance from the inland anchor: full-archive median WSE is ~63 m at 0 km, ~30 m at 15 km, ~2-3 m at 35 km, and tab1's own explainer places the coast at ~36 km. So <=18 km is the UPPER (inland) river and >18 km is the LOWER (coastal) river. The inversion originates in temporal_analysis.py lines 335-336, which name dist<=18 'downstream half (toward confluence/coast)'; the dashboard displays the misnamed keys with matching wrong labels.
failure_scenario: With the committed artifact, the table shows Kanektok 'Lower river (<=18 km)' = +0.009 m and 'Upper river (>18 km)' = -0.002 m, when the +0.009 value actually describes the upper/inland half and -0.002 the coastal half. Values are all within +/-0.02 m so the 'no typhoon signal' conclusion survives, but the row attributes each half-river change to the wrong half — and TEMPORAL_ANALYSIS.md carries the same inverted language.
suggested_fix: Fix the naming at the source (temporal_analysis.py: dist<=18 is upstream/inland, >18 is downstream/coastal), regenerate the JSON, and relabel the dashboard columns to match; or minimally swap the two column labels in the dashboard table.

title: Typhoon spatial-delta chart's fixed y-range clips the largest real WSE change (+0.68 m) while the caption claims the line 'hugs zero'
description: Chart 4 sets yaxis_range=[-0.5, 0.5] unconditionally. The committed temporal_q3_profile.parquet contains dwse up to +0.676 m: three Kanektok bins at 33.5, 34.0, 34.5 km are +0.528, +0.676, +0.538 m — beyond the axis, so their markers are cut off at the frame. The caption above the chart states 'the line stays flat and hugs zero — no spot along the river shows a storm scar', with no disclosure that the axis truncates the biggest excursion.
failure_scenario: Loaded temporal_results/temporal_q3_profile.parquet: 3 of 142 rows exceed |0.5| m (max +0.676 at 34.0 km). A reader of the tab sees a line exiting the top of the frame near the mouth but cannot see its peak, and is told the profile hugs zero everywhere. The excursion is at the tidal mouth (arguably tidal aliasing, and consistent with the 'damage was coastal' narrative), but it is hidden rather than shown-and-explained.
suggested_fix: Drop the fixed range (autoscale) or widen it to cover the data, and add a sentence noting the coastal-end excursion and its likely tidal origin; alternatively trim the tidal mouth as the fine-scale tab does (34 km) and say so.

title: Typhoon spatial-delta chart is the only distance-axis figure without the reversed x-axis convention
description: Every other figure with 'Distance from Anchor Point (km)' on x (tab1, tab2, tab3, tab4, fine-scale, all four DEM tabs) calls update_xaxes(autorange='reversed') so the coast reads on the left. fig_d in the Temporal tab (lines 3682-3703) plots the same axis un-reversed and still calls add_bifurcation_line(fig_d), so the bifurcation marker and the whole profile appear mirrored relative to the rest of the app.
failure_scenario: A user who has learned 'coast on the left, anchor on the right' from the other nine distance figures reads Chart 4's coastal-end feature (the 33-35 km bins) as being near the anchor/bifurcation, i.e. misplaces the only non-zero structure in the typhoon check to the wrong end of the river.
suggested_fix: Add fig_d.update_xaxes(autorange='reversed') for consistency.

title: Ice-season warning renders only in the data-load branch and vanishes on any subsequent rerun
description: The st.warning about ice-season passes (WSE 0.5-2+ m too high) is inside the `if "viz_df" not in st.session_state or viz_sig != selection_sig:` reload branch. On every later full rerun with the same selection (chart box-selection via on_select='rerun', Clear-highlight button, any button press) the cached else-branch runs and the warning is silently gone, while the ice-contaminated data remains plotted in every tab.
failure_scenario: User selects a Dec-Mar pass, sees the warning once, drags a box on the Gradient Profile (triggers on_select rerun) — the warning disappears for the rest of the session even though winter WSE readings are still in every chart and statistic.
suggested_fix: Compute ice_selected from selected_pass_dates outside the reload branch so the warning renders on every run.

title: 'Passes Analyzed' metric computed from the sampled viz_df undercounts small passes
description: The Summary Statistics footer shows viz_df['Pass_Date'].nunique(), but viz_df is the systematic 1-in-step sample (step = count/15000). A pass with fewer points than the step interval can lose all its rows, so the metric can disagree with the header's 'Viewing N passes' and with the selection.
failure_scenario: Ran the exact sampling query on the local archive with all 188 passes selected: count=7,895,912, step=526, sample nunique=184 vs 188 actual — the four smallest passes (e.g. 2024-03-27 with 42 rows, 2026-03-06 with 241) vanish. Header says 'Viewing 188 passes', footer says 'Passes Analyzed 184'. Does not trigger with the Select-All-(non-ice) button on current data (123=123) but does whenever ice passes or future sparse passes are included.
suggested_fix: Use COUNT(DISTINCT Pass_Date) from the same full-data SQL that produces `count`/stats_df, or use len(selected_pass_dates).

title: Detrended tab error/help text tells the user to switch a detrending method that no longer exists
description: detrend_method is hardcoded to 'Polynomial (2nd order)' (line 1320, comment 'Hardcoded detrending method'), but the poor-fit error block says 'Try: Switch to "Linear" or "LOESS" detrending method' (line 2525) and the 'How to read this graph' expander says 'the chosen baseline shape doesn't fit this data well — try a different one below' (line 2545). No selector exists anywhere on the page; the method_guidance dict (2553-2581) likewise documents four selectable options.
failure_scenario: If the mean residual ever exceeds 0.5 m (e.g. single-river selection), the red error instructs the user to use a control that is not rendered, and the expander points to a nonexistent widget 'below' — a dead-end instruction in a data-quality warning.
suggested_fix: Reword both passages to state the baseline is fixed to a 2nd-order polynomial, and drop the unused entries of method_guidance.

title: Detrended Residual map clips residuals at +/-3 m without disclosure
description: The map option uses Normalize(vmin=-3, vmax=3, clip=True), so any residual beyond +/-3 m renders as the same fully-saturated end color as a 3 m one. The file's own comment (lines 43-47) documents residual contamination 'tens of metres below the local trend' passing the ingestion filter, and unlike the Detrended Profile tab the map applies no residual-outlier flagging. Neither the colorbar nor the interpretation st.info mentions the cap.
failure_scenario: A spring-ice blob with residual -20 m displays identically to an ordinary -3 m point; a user comparing colors concludes the contamination is moderate. Only clicking the popup reveals the true value.
suggested_fix: Note the +/-3 m saturation in the colorbar caption/info text (e.g. 'Residual (m, capped at +/-3)'), or reuse flag_residual_outliers to style flagged points distinctly.

title: Dead code in the display layer: loess_smooth, avg_slope, unused correlation
description: Three computed-but-never-used items: (1) loess_smooth defined inside tab3 (line 2347) is never called — the LOESS path lives in calculate_detrending; (2) the summary stats SQL computes bin_slope/avg_slope (lines 1395/1401) but only avg_wse is ever displayed (line 3801), and the comment at 3798 says slope is intentionally excluded; (3) r = np.corrcoef(...) at line 3602 is computed per reach and never used (corr_txt only uses the median). compute_finescale_slope (line 517, just above the reviewed range) is likewise never called.
failure_scenario: No wrong output; maintenance hazard only — e.g. a future edit to the stats query's slope column would silently change nothing visible, and loess_smooth diverging from calculate_detrending's LOESS would go unnoticed.
suggested_fix: Delete loess_smooth, the bin_slope/avg_slope columns, and the unused corrcoef; delete or use compute_finescale_slope.

title: D7: calculate_slope_profile smooths across coverage gaps as if adjacent — up to ~280 cm/km slope distortion on sparse selections
description: calculate_slope_profile bins WSE to 100 m bins via groupby (line 259), which drops empty bins, then applies gaussian_filter1d with sigma_bins = smooth_km/bin_size (lines 266-267). gaussian_filter1d operates in INDEX space, so the 2 km kernel is only 2 km where bins are contiguous; across a coverage gap, non-adjacent bins are treated as adjacent and the effective physical kernel stretches/compresses, and np.interp at line 271 then linearly bridges the gap. The identical port exists in thesis_figures/core.py:180.
failure_scenario: I scanned all 354 (pass, reach) combos in the local archive: 120 have gaps >0.1 km in the pooled 100 m bin series (max single gap 2.3 km). Comparing the coded smoothing to gap-aware smoothing (fill to a regular grid, interpolate, smooth): selecting the single pass 2026-04-18 (non-ice) on Uyak Creek gives median slope error 43.7 cm/km and max 278 cm/km — larger than the river's true ~190 cm/km gradient — in the Slope Profile tab (line 2714) and in the map's 'Interval Slope' coloring (line 1449). Mitigations found: the DEFAULT 4-recent-pass selection and the all-pass pool have ZERO gaps (verified), and the thesis figure (make_figures.py:839) runs on the pooled open-water archive, also gap-free — so no published number is currently wrong; the distortion appears only for sparse dashboard selections, which the welcome page allows (single-pass selection is normal use, and 2026-04-18 is outside the ice-season warning months).
suggested_fix: Reindex the binned medians onto a complete 0.1 km grid before smoothing (NaN-aware or interpolate with a gap limit, as _fine_regular_grid already does), or blank the output across gaps wider than the kernel. Apply the same fix to thesis_figures/core.py:calculate_slope_profile.

title: D18: beta_floodplain.py depends on unversioned /tmp inputs — the documented ArcGIS β reproduction is irreproducible
description: GDB = "/tmp/clean_and_complete.gdb" (line 37) and the validation overlay reads "/tmp/original_beta.parquet" (line 147; run_B.py:189 reads the same path). Neither file exists now (verified: both absent), /tmp is volatile, and neither is tracked or documented with a recovery path in the repo. AVULSION_ANALYSIS.md:33 and :142 cite clean_and_complete.gdb as the source of the recovered ArcGIS result, and STATUS.md:98 cites beta_floodplain.py as the script that 'demonstrated the artifact'.
failure_scenario: Anyone (including the author, post-reboot) running `python3 DEM_Transects/beta_floodplain.py` to reproduce the writeup's two-zone β result gets an immediate failure opening /tmp/clean_and_complete.gdb; the provenance chain for a number cited in the thesis writeup is broken. The production arc pipeline (build_arc_B.py) is unaffected.
suggested_fix: Move the recovered .gdb (or an exported GeoPackage of Avulsion_Lines_2/Guide_Lines_2) and original_beta.parquet into DEM_Transects/data/ or DEM_Transects/reference/ (they are small), or document the exact recovery procedure and update the paths.

title: D21: hardcoded '~0.34 m' differential-stage artifact is not reproducible from the committed artifact (recomputation gives 0.27–0.48 m); other hardcoded helptext numbers verified current
description: The Cross-Sections helptext hardcodes ~15 numeric results. I verified the key ones against the current DEM_Transects/data/arcB_channels.parquet and they are CURRENT: 'within ~0.15 m of the SWOT median' (actual: Kanektok -0.147 m, Uyak +0.138 m), snap offsets '~38 m / ~12 m' (37.7 / 12.0 m), '~9% of arcs' at the search wall (9.4% Kanektok), stage moves '~0.7 m' (p90-p10 median 0.72/0.64 m), 'H_AR median ≈ +0.1 m' (0.141 m — borderline; rounds to 0.1 only at 1 decimal), and line 2911's '~3.6 cm/km' reach-average advantage (gated reference gradient: 195.36 - 191.73 = 3.64). The one figure that does NOT reproduce is the '~0.34 m of spurious Uyak-higher' stage artifact (dashboard comment line 891; also swot_arc_reference.py:24, build_arc_B.py:364, STATUS.md:23, AVULSION_ANALYSIS.md:72): from arcB_channels.parquet the per-arc artifact median((uyak_dem-uyak_swotmed)-(kan_dem-kan_swotmed)) = +0.27 m, and DEM-diff-median minus paired-diff-median = 1.445 - 0.963 = +0.48 m. 0.34 may come from the original full-stage-distribution estimator (29th/76th percentile claim is qualitatively consistent), but it cannot be recomputed from any committed artifact.
failure_scenario: A rebuild of arcB_channels.parquet (e.g. after a CREST_WIN_M or snap-window change) silently invalidates every hardcoded number in the ~65-line expander at lines 996-1061 with no test or generation step tying them to the artifact; and today, a reader trying to verify the ~0.34 m figure in AVULSION_ANALYSIS.md against the committed data gets 0.27-0.48 m, not 0.34 m.
suggested_fix: Compute the displayed summary numbers from the loaded parquet (most already have the columns) instead of hardcoding, or add a build-time assertion script; for the 0.34 m figure, either recompute it in swot_arc_reference.py and print it (so provenance is rerunnable) or restate it as the reproducible 0.27 m per-arc median.

title: D3: stale detrend UI — error text recommends switching methods that no longer exist; 3 of 4 guidance branches unreachable (reachable branch OK)
description: detrend_method is hardcoded to "Polynomial (2nd order)" at line 1320 (no selector exists). The poor-fit error at lines 2517-2526 still says 'Try: Switch to "Linear" or "LOESS" detrending method', and line 2545's expander says 'try a different one below' — both impossible. method_guidance (2553-2581) has 4 branches; only "2nd Order Polynomial" is reachable. I checked the seed's key-mismatch concern: the reachable branch's key DOES match method_name returned by calculate_detrending ('2nd Order Polynomial'), so st.success at 2583 renders real guidance today. However there is a latent mismatch: the "Linear" key would never match method_name "Linear Fit" (calculate_detrending line 152), so re-enabling Linear would render an empty green success box.
failure_scenario: A user whose selection yields |mean residual| > 0.5 m (e.g. a single-river ice-season pass) is told to switch to a Linear/LOESS method that has no UI control — a dead-end instruction; and any future re-enable of "Linear" hits the 'Linear' vs 'Linear Fit' key mismatch and shows blank guidance.
suggested_fix: Rewrite the error text for the fixed method; collapse method_guidance to the one reachable entry (or key it on the `method` argument, not method_name).

title: D11: len(selected_reaches)!=2 gate is dead, but the single-river detrend warning is NOT dead — 22 of 188 passes image only one river
description: selected_reaches = available_reaches at line 1287, and available_reaches is SELECT DISTINCT Reach_Name (line 1121), which always returns both rivers for this dataset — so the len(selected_reaches) != 2 gate at line 2221 can never fire (benign defensive dead path). The second half of the seed is REFUTED: the num_rivers == 1 warning at lines 2402-2404 is keyed on baseline_df['Reach_Name'].nunique(), which is DATA-dependent — I verified 22 of 188 passes in the archive contain only one river (e.g. 2023-11-22, 2024-09-30, 2025-08-30), so selecting only such passes legitimately triggers it. Its wording ('Single river selected') misdescribes the cause (coverage, not selection), since river selection no longer exists.
failure_scenario: No wrong output. The 2221 branch is unreachable scaffolding; the 2402 warning fires correctly but tells a user who selected one single-river-coverage pass that they 'selected' a single river, which they cannot un-do via any control.
suggested_fix: Drop the 2221 gate or keep as assertion; reword the 2402 warning to 'only one river has data in the selected passes'.

title: D4: two coexisting 2nd-order detrend fits (map coloring vs Detrended tab) disagree by up to ~9 cm at the default selection
description: The map's detrended_residual is fit on viz_df (≤15,000 systematically sampled rows, lines 1434-1439) while the Detrended tab fits on the load_detrend_frame sample (≤~30,000 rows, different ORDER BY tie-breakers, lines 210-228). Two different samples → two different polynomials → the same physical point carries two different residuals.
failure_scenario: Measured on real data: at the default selection (4 most recent passes, 140,597 rows; viz n=15,621, tab n=35,149) the two baselines differ by median 1.4 cm, max 8.6 cm over 0.3-70 km; for the all-non-ice selection max 1.0 cm; all passes max 2.9 cm. A point can therefore show e.g. residual +0.312 m in the tab hover and +0.256 m in the map popup. Against the map's ±3 m color scale and the ~1 m inter-river signal this is visually and scientifically negligible — real but benign-to-low.
suggested_fix: Reuse load_detrend_frame's baseline coefficients (fit once, predict on viz_df) so both views share one baseline.

title: D20: superelevation and diff metrics silently fall back to DEM-stage values with no flag column (currently inert: 0 arcs use the fallback)
description: kan/uyak_superelev_m = superelev_med_m.fillna(superelev_dem_m) (lines 383-384) mixes SWOT-median-stage values with DEM-mosaic-stage values in one column with no indicator of which stage a row carries; dashboard line 901 does the same for the Uyak-Kanektok metric (falls back to dem_diff when swot_diff is NaN — the help text does disclose the DEM value, but the headline number switches meaning silently). Verified against the current artifact: all 64 arcs have swot_diff, and 0 of 63 fp-valid arcs lack superelev_med — so no displayed value is currently a fallback.
failure_scenario: Latent: if swot_arc_reference.parquet is rebuilt with fewer qualifying passes (MIN_PASSES=8 gate) some radii lose their SWOT stage distribution, and those arcs' 'superelevation at the median observed stage' metrics silently become DEM-blend-stage numbers (~0.3 m different per the stage-artifact analysis) with nothing in the parquet or UI marking them.
suggested_fix: Add a boolean 'stage_source' / '*_is_dem_stage' column when filling, and have the dashboard annotate fallback values.

title: D12: stats_df avg_slope computed per selection then deliberately never shown
description: The stats query computes MEDIAN(slope_calc) per 1 km bin and AVG(bin_slope) AS avg_slope (lines 1395, 1401) on the FULL selection, but the summary table keeps only avg_wse (lines 3798-3805) with an explicit comment that a per-selection average slope is density-biased and intentionally excluded. The avg_slope column is referenced nowhere else.
failure_scenario: No wrong output — the exclusion is scientifically correct and documented. Cost is one extra aggregate over up to ~7.9M rows per selection change; benign.
suggested_fix: Drop bin_slope/avg_slope from the query, keeping the comment explaining why slope is not offered here.

title: D5: map Classification legend provisions classes 5-7 that cannot occur (ingestion keeps 3-4 only); prose says Classes 3-4
description: class_colors at lines 3238-3241 defines colors for classes 3-7, but the archive verifiably contains only classes 3 (3,846,474 rows) and 4 (4,049,438 rows) — I confirmed with a GROUP BY over the master parquets. The prose at line 3833 correctly says 'SWOT Classes 3-4'. The loop at 3243-3246 skips empty classes, so no phantom layers render — the extra entries are inert config, but they contradict the documented filter and imply to a maintainer that classes 5-7 can appear.
failure_scenario: No wrong output today. If a future ingestion change reintroduced classes 5-7, the map would silently render them as valid 'high-quality water' with no warning — but as written it is purely misleading dead config.
suggested_fix: Trim class_colors to {3, 4} (matching ingestion and the line-3833 prose).

title: D6: fine-grid pos = ix-1 would silently drop a bin at ibin 0 — no real data can reach it (min dist_km = 0.30)
description: compute_finescale_pass_matrix builds grid = np.arange(1, imax+1)*0.1 (line 406) and maps pass bins with pos = ix-1 masked by pos >= 0 (lines 414-415), so a pass bin at ibin=0 (dist 0-0.05 km) would be dropped without warning. Verified against the archive: the minimum dist_km is 0.3003 km (Kanektok) / 0.3013 km (Uyak) — the smallest possible ibin is 3, and zero rows land in ibin 0 (checked pre- and post- npix>=30 gate). The distance is radial-from-anchor with rivers starting ~0.3 km out, so this is structurally unreachable, not just currently empty.
failure_scenario: None with this dataset. Only a future dataset with points within 50 m of the anchor would lose its first bin silently.
suggested_fix: Start the grid at the data's min ibin (grid = arange(ibin_min, imax+1)) or assert ibin >= 1.

title: D14: z==0 masking in sample_arc loses zero real pixels — and is the mechanism that catches out-of-bounds samples (benign, load-bearing)
description: Seed suspected z==0 masking on the PGC raster (nodata -9999) could discard real near-sea-level terrain. Verified empirically: a full block scan of batch_outputs/arcticdem_rivers_2m.tif (175.7M pixels, float32, nodata -9999) found 0 pixels equal to -9999, 0 pixels exactly 0.0, and 0 pixels in (0, 5) — the raster's heights are ellipsoidal (~+13 m at sea level; min orthometric elevation in arcB_profiles.parquet is +0.14 m, i.e. raw ~13.6), so exact-0 cannot be real terrain here. Moreover, rasterio's boundless sample() returns 0 for points OUTSIDE the raster extent, and 23.1% of the 481,678 arc samples are NaN — dominated by off-raster arc sweep — meaning the z==0 mask is what correctly rejects those out-of-bounds fills.
failure_scenario: None: exact loss of real data is zero (counted). Removing the z==0 mask as 'wrong for PGC nodata' would be the actual bug — out-of-bounds samples would enter as 0 m ellipsoidal = -13.5 m orthometric terrain.
suggested_fix: Keep the mask; update the inline comment to say 0 also marks rasterio boundless out-of-extent fill (the '0 = GEE fill' rationale in beta_floodplain.py:56 is stale for this raster).

title: D15: R_EARTH 6371.0088 vs 6371.0 across scripts — 5 cm max over the 35 km domain; BIFURCATION_DIST_KM=2.493 verified correct
description: build_arc_B.py/adcp_depth_stats.py use R=6371.0088 km; DEM_Pull.py:34 and SWOT_Pull.py use 6371.0. The relative difference is 1.38e-6: over the 35 km arc domain the distance discrepancy is 0.048 m (0.10 m at 70 km) — three orders of magnitude below the 0.5 km arc spacing and the 100 m analysis bins. Recomputed the anchor→bifurcation haversine: 2.493114 km (R=6371.0088) vs 2.493111 km (R=6371.0), both rounding to the constant 2.493 in dashboard_swot.py:54 — verified correct.
failure_scenario: None measurable: a SWOT dist_km and an arc R_km for the same physical point differ by <5 cm, far inside every bin width used. Benign inconsistency only.
suggested_fix: Optionally standardize on one radius constant in a shared module; no numerical consequence.

title: D16: geoid comment endpoints (13.77/13.27) are R=0/coast extrapolations, not the artifact's actual endpoints (13.74 at R=3, 13.28 at R=34.5)
description: Comments at build_arc_B.py:24 and :194-195 (and swot_arc_reference.py:11) say EGM2008 'runs 13.77 m at the anchor to 13.27 m at the coast'. The committed artifact swot_arc_reference.parquet spans R=3.0-34.5 km with geoid_m 13.7386 at R=3.0 and 13.2802 at R=34.5 (verified). 13.77/13.27 describe values extrapolated to R=0 and beyond the last arc; the numbers actually applied to any arc are 13.74-13.28. Values differ by ≤3 cm and the geoid cancels in all within-arc quantities.
failure_scenario: No numeric effect on any computed quantity. A reader auditing the artifact against the comment sees 13.74/13.28 and may suspect a datum error where none exists.
suggested_fix: Reword to 'from ~13.74 m at the innermost arc (R=3 km; ~13.77 m extrapolated to the anchor) to ~13.28 m at the outermost'.

title: D17: 'ADCP median 1.30 m' comment verified accurate — seed's 1.22/1.29 not reproduced (benign)
description: Seed claimed the comment's 'ADCP median 1.30 m' conflicts with stats of median 1.22 / mean 1.29. Verified against DEM_Transects/data/kanektok_thalweg_depth.parquet: 17,141 pings, raw median 1.314 m, mean 1.367 m; the per-arc binned depth actually used by the pipeline (kan_depth_m in arcB_channels.parquet) has median 1.299 m — which is exactly what '1.30 m' states. The suspected 1.22/1.29 figures do not appear in any committed artifact I checked; they may come from a differently-filtered adcp_depth_stats.py run (that script reads the raw ~/Downloads ADCP folder, not present).
failure_scenario: None — the comment's number matches the data at the precision quoted (1.299 ≈ 1.30; raw-ping median 1.31 differs by 1 cm). Reporting the seed as benign rather than dropping it.
suggested_fix: None required; optionally state which estimator the 1.30 refers to (per-arc binned median).

title: D19: avulsion_metrics.py docstring claims 'production core' but production computes β inline twice; module used only by the validation harness
description: The docstring says 'This is the production core of the DEM_Transects analysis', but the only importer is validation/validate_against_gearon.py:23. The two production scripts compute β inline: build_arc_B.py:319-322 (kHAR/kHM with a kHM>0 guard) and beta_floodplain.py:70-72 (har/hm with hm>0 guard). The inline math matches ridge_height/channel_depth/superelevation (H_AR/H_M), so the Gearon-validated port does not actually protect the numbers that ship — a future edit to the inline formulas would not be caught by the validation harness.
failure_scenario: No current numeric divergence (formulas verified equivalent, and the inline versions add NaN/positivity guards the module lacks). Risk is process-level: the validated module and the shipped computation can drift apart silently, defeating the stated purpose of the validation harness.
suggested_fix: Either have build_arc_B.py call avulsion_metrics.superelevation (keeping its guards) or fix the docstring to say the module exists for validation parity, with the inline formulas as the production copies.

title: D10: unused imports (gc, MeasureControl) and a stale 51 KB dashboard_swot.py.backup
description: import gc (line 10, commented 'Memory management') has zero uses ('gc.' matches nothing). from folium.plugins import MeasureControl (line 13) is unused — both call sites use plugins.MeasureControl (lines 2054, 3197). dashboard_swot.py.backup (51,828 bytes, mtime Feb 23) is a stale snapshot of a much older version of the now-3,868-line file, sitting untracked-risk in the repo root.

suggested_fix: Delete the two imports and the .backup file (git history preserves the old version).

title: D9: calculate_detrending returns polynomial coefficients in numpy's scaled domain — never surfaced anywhere (benign)
description: For the polynomial branches, coeffs = poly.coef (lines 156, 161) are the coefficients in np.polynomial.Polynomial.fit's internal shifted/scaled domain, not physical dist_km units — misleading if ever displayed or used for slope. Verified both call sites discard them: load_detrend_frame line 227 binds _coeffs, and the map-metrics call at line 1434 binds _. The thesis port (thesis_figures/core.py) also returns and discards them identically.
failure_scenario: None today. Latent only: a future feature printing 'baseline coefficients' or computing d(baseline)/dx from coeffs would report values wrong by the domain scaling (~35x on the linear term for a 0-70 km domain).
suggested_fix: Return poly.convert().coef (physical-domain coefficients) or return None with a comment.

title: D22: CH_WIN_M=250.0 duplicated between dashboard and build script, tied only by a comment
description: dashboard_swot.py:836 hardcodes CH_WIN_M = 250.0 with comment 'matches build_arc_B.py' (authoritative constant at build_arc_B.py:91). The dashboard value only draws the green 'floodplain corridor' vrect (lines 839-842); the fp_ref_m metric itself is precomputed in the parquet with the build-side constant.
failure_scenario: If build_arc_B.py's CH_WIN_M is retuned (as CREST_WIN_M was, 350→150) and artifacts rebuilt, the dashboard's shaded corridor would no longer depict the zone the displayed fp_ref_m/superelevation numbers were computed over — a visual/numeric mismatch with no error. Currently consistent (both 250.0).
suggested_fix: Write ch_win_m as a column (or a one-row metadata table) into arcB_channels.parquet and have the dashboard read it.

title: rebuild_master.py bypasses the KNOWN_BAD_PASSES exclusion and skips the reference-gradient rebuild
description: SWOT_Pull.py's rebuild_master_from_daily_csvs() (SWOT_Pull.py:488-495) drops KNOWN_BAD_PASSES (2025-04-17, spring-breakup ice) before writing master_all_data.{csv,parquet} and the partitions, and then recomputes reference_gradient_per_pass.parquet from the filtered frame. The standalone rebuild_master.py — the exact utility README.md section 'Rebuild Without Re-downloading' (README.md:114-120) tells users to run — imports only KEEP_COLUMNS and ROWS_PER_CHUNK from SWOT_Pull (rebuild_master.py:14), concatenates ALL daily CSVs with no exclusion (line 40), and never calls compute_reference_gradient(). The daily checkpoint batch_outputs/data/2025-04-17_data.csv exists (kept intentionally for provenance), so the documented-bad pass would be re-included. dashboard_swot.py and temporal_analysis.py have no exclusion registry of their own (they deliberately inherit it from ingestion, per DASHBOARD_TODO item 6); only thesis_figures is protected by its own config.EXCLUDED_PASSES applied in core.py.
failure_scenario: User runs `python rebuild_master.py` (as README advertises, e.g. after changing KEEP_COLUMNS). The 2025-04-17 ice pass (~10.8k rows; reach gradients 236/224 cm/km vs medians ~192/196) silently re-enters master_all_data_part_*.parquet, which dashboard_swot.py and temporal_analysis.py read unfiltered — means/bands/extremes on the dashboard and any re-run temporal stats are contaminated by the pass that was formally QC-excluded. Meanwhile reference_gradient_per_pass.parquet is left stale (not rebuilt), desynchronized from the new master. Verified: batch_outputs/data/2025-04-17_data.csv is present; current parts contain 0 rows for that date only because SWOT_Pull's own rebuild was used.
suggested_fix: Have rebuild_master.py import and apply KNOWN_BAD_PASSES (or just call SWOT_Pull.rebuild_master_from_daily_csvs() instead of duplicating it), and call compute_reference_gradient(final_df) at the end.

title: README describes a sidebar, controls, tabs and remote dataset that no longer exist in the dashboard
description: Multiple README claims diverge from dashboard_swot.py: (1) 'Sidebar Controls' (lines 163-169: date range slider, river selection, detrending method choice Linear/Poly/LOESS, theme toggle) — the code has NO st.sidebar at all; pass selection is welcome-page checkboxes (dashboard_swot.py:1168-1203), rivers are always both (line 1288 'Always include both rivers'), detrend_method is hardcoded to 'Polynomial (2nd order)' (line 1320), plotly template hardcoded 'plotly_white' (line 1323). (2) Line 221 'Users can uncheck "Exclude ice season" in the sidebar' — no such checkbox exists; ice passes get a ❄️ label and a warning banner, and the default selection is simply the 4 most recent passes regardless of season (_select_passes n=4, line 1173), so 'excludes Dec-Mar data by default' (line 220) is also not literally true. (3) Tab tables (lines 130-161) omit the 'Hydraulic Gradient' and 'Fine-Scale Slope' SWOT tabs and the DEM 'Cross-Sections' tab (dashboard_swot.py:1473-1476, 1775-1780), and the described top-level/'More Tabs' structure was replaced by SWOT Data / DEM Data main tabs. (4) Line 134 says Gradient Profile shows 'linear regression trendlines ... cm/km' — the OLS trendline was replaced by a binned-median profile + Theil-Sen reference header (dashboard_swot.py:1548-1556). (5) Lines 39 and 75 say the remote dataset is 'Apr-Jul 2025 + Apr-May 2026, 1.38M points, 29 passes' — the current dashboard_data.parquet build artifact (2026-07-14) has 2,402,739 rows, 60 passes, 2023-07-31..2026-07-09 (also confirmed by thesis_figures/config.py:33 'dashboard_data.parquet holds only ~60' passes); docs/development_notes.md:330 repeats the stale 1.38M/42MB claim as 'currently'.
failure_scenario: A collaborator or thesis committee member reads the README to operate or audit the dashboard, looks for the sidebar ice-exclusion checkbox or tries to switch detrending to LOESS, and finds none of it — or cites '29 passes / 1.38M points' for the public app when it actually serves 60 passes spanning the full archive.
suggested_fix: Rewrite the 'Sidebar Controls' section as welcome-page pass selection, update the tab tables (add Hydraulic Gradient, Fine-Scale Slope, Cross-Sections), state the hardcoded 2nd-order polynomial detrend, and refresh the remote-dataset description.

title: SCIENTIFIC_METHODOLOGY.md states the study reach is ~70 km and that 0 km is 'the confluence where rivers meet'
description: The methodology document that backs the thesis states 'Our Study Area: Maximum distance ~70 km (coast to confluence)' (line 586) and 'Coordinate Convention: 0 km = Confluence (where rivers meet); ~70 km = River mouth (coast)' (lines 598-599). Verified against the data: max dist_km is 36.09 km (Uyak) / 35.07 km (Kanektok); README.md:214 already carries the corrected '~36 km = coast'. Also, 0 km is the ANCHOR point ~2.49 km upriver of the BIFURCATION where the channels diverge — not a confluence where rivers meet (this is DASHBOARD_TODO item 4, still open). The same stale ~70 km appears in a dashboard code comment (dashboard_swot.py:42 '~70 km downstream gradient') and docs/development_notes.md:45; SWOT_Pull.py:78 still labels the anchor 'THE CONFLUENCE ANCHOR'. The section's implementation pointers are also stale: 'SWOT_Pull.py, lines 31-34 (constants) and lines 42-51 (function)' (line 553) — actual locations are lines 81-82 and 104-119.
failure_scenario: Methods text copied from this document into the thesis (its stated purpose) would claim a 70 km study reach and a confluence at 0 km; both are factually wrong (36 km; anchor upriver of a bifurcation) and directly contradict Figure captions/README built from the corrected convention. The Haversine error-budget justification ('<0.5% at ~70 km') is argued against the wrong length scale.
suggested_fix: Replace ~70 km with ~36 km in lines 586 and 599, change 'Confluence (where rivers meet)' to 'anchor point (~2.5 km upriver of the bifurcation)', fix the SWOT_Pull.py line references, and rename SWOT_Pull.py's 'CONFLUENCE ANCHOR' comment.

title: DEPLOYMENT.md / NEXT_STEPS.md / DEPLOYMENT_SUMMARY.md document a retired Git-LFS deployment and wrong runtime constants
description: All three deployment docs describe committing batch_outputs/master_all_data_part_*.parquet to the repo via Git LFS ('.gitattributes for LFS tracking', 162.5 MB, 68 files; DEPLOYMENT.md:19-23, NEXT_STEPS.md whole file, DEPLOYMENT_SUMMARY.md:60-69). Reality: .gitattributes contains only '*.parquet binary' (a linguist override, no LFS filter), `git ls-files batch_outputs/` is empty, and the actual deployment reads dashboard_data.parquet from GitHub Release v2.0-data via DuckDB httpfs (dashboard_swot.py:27-29, 596; development_notes.md:330 documents this switch). Constants are also wrong: 'Limited baseline queries to 50k points' and 'MAX_BASELINE_POINTS (currently 50k)' vs code 30000 (dashboard_swot.py:31); 'DuckDB memory limit to 800MB' vs code SET memory_limit='600MB' (dashboard_swot.py:615); 'All 6 tabs work (Gradient, Elevation Diff, Detrended, Interval Slopes, Map, Raw Data)' vs 9 SWOT tabs + 6 DEM tabs, and the 'Interval Slopes' tab was renamed 'Slope Profile' in 2026-03. DEPLOYMENT.md:230-234 further advises recovering by diff/restore against dashboard_swot.py.backup — a 1,227-line February snapshot vs the current 3,868-line file, so following that advice would revert ~6 months of scientific fixes (reference gradient, QC exclusion, cross-sections).
failure_scenario: A teammate onboarding from DEPLOYMENT.md installs git-lfs, tries `git lfs track`/`git lfs push` against a repo with no LFS config, or 'fixes' a memory crash by restoring dashboard_swot.py.backup, silently discarding the Theil-Sen reference-gradient tab, KNOWN_BAD_PASSES handling, and the SWOT/DEM tab structure.
suggested_fix: Rewrite (or clearly mark as historical) the three deployment docs around the GitHub-Release + httpfs flow, correct 30000/600MB, and delete or date-stamp dashboard_swot.py.backup.

title: Declared streamlit floor (>=1.35 / >=1.28) does not support the width="stretch" API the dashboard uses
description: requirements.txt pins streamlit>=1.35.0 ('>=1.35 for st.plotly_chart(on_select=...)') and requirements-full.txt pins streamlit>=1.28.0 (README.md:34 presents requirements-full as sufficient to run the dashboard). But dashboard_swot.py now calls st.plotly_chart(..., width="stretch") and st.dataframe(..., width="stretch") at 10+ sites (lines 1597, 1759, 2197, 2306, 2497, 2627, 2681, 2755, 2781, 2897) — the string-width layout API introduced in the 2025 Streamlit releases (~1.49) that deprecated use_container_width; it does not exist in 1.35, let alone 1.28. The installed env is 1.52.2 so it works today, but the declared floors are a false compatibility claim. The file also mixes both APIs (use_container_width at lines 882, 965, 1711, ... alongside width="stretch"), so no single version cleanly matches the code without deprecation warnings.
failure_scenario: An environment that resolves streamlit to any version in the allowed range below the width-API release (e.g. another dependency pins streamlit<1.45, or a cached 1.35 wheel satisfies the requirement) launches the dashboard and every chart/table call with width="stretch" raises (unexpected keyword / invalid width value), breaking most tabs while requirements.txt claims the version is supported.
suggested_fix: Raise the floor in requirements.txt (and the dashboard note in README.md:138) to the first streamlit release supporting width="stretch", and either bump requirements-full.txt's streamlit to match or stop advertising it as dashboard-capable.

title: swot_arc_reference.py uses a Classes 3-7 filter labelled 'validated' and a stale fallback parquet that still contains the QC-excluded pass
description: CLASS_MIN, CLASS_MAX = 3, 7 with comment 'validated SWOT water-classification filter' contradicts the project-wide methodology: SWOT_Pull.py DEFAULT_CLASSES=[3,4], and SCIENTIFIC_METHODOLOGY.md:267-274 explicitly documents that Classes 5-7 are EXCLUDED (the 3-7 range is the superseded early filter). It is currently a no-op only because the primary input dashboard_data.parquet already contains only classes 3-4 (verified). Separately, SWOT_CANDIDATES (lines 49-52) falls back to swot_apr_jul_2025_2026.parquet when dashboard_data.parquet is absent — verified that this older subset still contains 10,794 rows of the QC-excluded ice pass 2025-04-17 (the registry pass in SWOT_Pull.KNOWN_BAD_PASSES / config.EXCLUDED_PASSES), and this script applies no pass exclusion and no ice-month gate of its own.
failure_scenario: Regenerating the committed data/swot_arc_reference.parquet on a machine where only the old subset exists (both files are gitignored) rebuilds the per-arc SWOT stage medians/p10/p90 and pass-paired Uyak-minus-Kanektok differences INCLUDING the documented spring-breakup ice pass — those numbers feed the dashboard Cross-Sections tab's superelevation-at-stage display, i.e. a thesis-relevant validation figure, and nothing would flag the contamination. Pointing the script at a raw classes-3-7 archive would additionally admit dark-water pixels the methodology says are excluded.
suggested_fix: Change the filter to classes 3-4 (or import DEFAULT_CLASSES), drop or refresh the stale fallback, and apply the KNOWN_BAD_PASSES/EXCLUDED_PASSES registry before aggregating.

title: DASHBOARD_TODO.md still lists items 2, 3 and 6 as open although they are implemented
description: Of the deferred items, only item 1 is marked RESOLVED, but: item 2 (replace the density-biased OLS trendline on Gradient Profile) is done — dashboard_swot.py:1548-1582 now draws the binned-median profile with a percentile band and shows the Theil-Sen reference gradient above the chart instead of an OLS slope; item 3 (fix stale '~70 km = coast' in README) is done — README.md:214 now reads '~36 km = coast'; item 6 (propagate the 2025-04-17 exclusion) is done — SWOT_Pull.py:70-76 has the documented KNOWN_BAD_PASSES registry applied at master rebuild and inherited by the reference-gradient artifact.
