suggested_fix: Strike items 2, 3 and 6 as resolved (with commit refs) and leave 4 and 5 as the open set.

title: Methodology summary claims 'Dashboard warnings for Oct-May'; the dashboard warns only for Dec-Mar
description: The verification-summary table says 'Ice Season Handling ... Dashboard warnings for Oct-May', but dashboard_swot.py flags/warns only for months (12, 1, 2, 3) (_is_ice at line 1156-1158, warning banner at 1346-1355). The doc's own ice table (lines 294-299: open water Jun-Sep, caution Oct-Nov and Apr-May) is also in tension with the locked analysis window used everywhere else — REFGRAD_OPEN_WATER_MONTHS = Apr-Nov (SWOT_Pull.py:59, temporal_analysis.py:67, thesis_figures/core.py:29), a choice line 709 of the same document endorses and temporal analysis empirically validated (shoulder months = 27% of gated passes). README.md:218 states Oct-Nov are empirically ice-free.
failure_scenario: A reviewer cross-checking the methodology document against the app finds Apr/May/Oct/Nov passes presented with no warning despite the doc's claim, or conversely questions why Apr-Nov data enters the reference gradient when the doc's table marks Apr-May/Oct-Nov 'caution' — an avoidable credibility hit in a document whose purpose is verification.
suggested_fix: Change line 32 to 'Dashboard warnings for Dec-Mar' and add a sentence reconciling the conservative table with the empirically validated Apr-Nov analysis window.

title: .streamlit/config.toml comment mislabels #1f77b4 as 'Dodger blue (matches Uyak Creek)'
description: primaryColor = "#1f77b4" is matplotlib tab-blue; the Uyak Creek color used everywhere in the project is CSS dodgerblue = #1E90FF (dashboard_swot.py:57-60, thesis_figures/config.py:81-84, DEM_Transects/make_avulsion_figures.py:99). The theme accent therefore does NOT match the Uyak series color despite the comment claiming pixel-consistency was the intent.
failure_scenario: Someone screenshotting the dashboard for the thesis/poster (the [theme] section's stated purpose) assumes UI accent = Uyak color per the comment; buttons/sliders render #1f77b4 next to #1E90FF chart traces, a visible mismatch.
suggested_fix: Set primaryColor = "#1E90FF" or fix the comment.

title: requirements.txt claims tqdm is 'used by dashboard loading indicator' but the dashboard never imports it
description: The dashboard-only requirements file includes 'tqdm>=4.65.0  # Progress bars (used by dashboard loading indicator)'. dashboard_swot.py contains no tqdm import or usage (grep confirms zero hits); loading feedback uses st.spinner/st.toast. tqdm is genuinely used only by the ingestion side (SWOT_Pull.py, rebuild_master.py), which is covered by requirements-full.txt. The other unusual entries are fine: matplotlib IS used (colormaps, dashboard_swot.py:15-16), and branca/jinja2 (imported at lines 18-19) arrive transitively via folium/streamlit.
failure_scenario: Streamlit Cloud installs an unnecessary package on every deploy, and a maintainer auditing dependencies is told a false reason to keep it; if someone 'trusts the comment' and adds a tqdm-based indicator assuming one exists, they chase a phantom feature.
suggested_fix: Drop the tqdm line from requirements.txt (keep it in requirements-full.txt), or fix the comment to say it is not a dashboard dependency.

title: Geoid hull fallback puts up to 0.34 m datum error into 36,803 DEM profile points, concentrated at the Uyak mouth
description: build_geoid_interpolator() builds a LinearNDInterpolator over the convex hull of (subsampled) SWOT pixel locations; every DEM pixel outside that hull silently gets the constant FALLBACK_GEOID = 13.46 m. The out-of-hull points are not scattered — they are exactly where the geoid deviates most from 13.46: rebuilding the interpolator from batch_outputs/data/*.csv and applying it to dem_river_elevations.parquet shows 36,803/2,485,204 points (1.48%) get the fallback, 34,600 of them at Uyak dist_km 32-36 (true geoid ~13.21 m, so wse biased LOW by ~0.25 m) and ~1,900 at dist_km 0-1 (true geoid ~13.79 m, wse biased HIGH by ~0.33 m). The 0.5 km binned-median profile the dashboard draws is contaminated: the terminal Uyak bin at 36.0 km is 84% fallback points and its median is 0.24 m too low (measured: 1.739 m vs corrected 1.982 m); bins 33.5-35.5 are 12-33% contaminated. Any per-point DEM-vs-SWOT residual analysis over the coastal Uyak reach inherits a systematic ~0.25 m tilt.
failure_scenario: Ran DEM_Pull's interpolator rebuild against batch_outputs/data CSVs and evaluated on dem_river_elevations.parquet: 36,803 NaN (out-of-hull) points; nearest-grid true geoid gives fallback error median +0.247 m at the coast, -0.336 m at the anchor. Recomputing the Uyak 36.0 km bin median with the corrected geoid shifts it +0.243 m — the published DEM profile's last bin shows an artificial ~0.24 m dip at the river mouth.
suggested_fix: Replace the constant fallback with nearest-neighbour extrapolation of the SWOT geoid grid (e.g. scipy.interpolate.NearestNDInterpolator for out-of-hull points), or clamp out-of-hull points to the nearest hull value; the geoid is smooth so NN extrapolation is accurate to <2 cm here.

title: Example arc cross-sections are captured at R-0.5 km but labeled R (banker's rounding on the 0.5 km grid)
description: `if int(round(R)) in example_R and int(round(R)) not in examples` iterates radii in 0.5 km steps, and round-half-to-even maps 7.5->8, 15.5->16, 23.5->24, 31.5->32. Since 7.5 is visited before 8.0 (and the dict-guard blocks the later, correct radius), all four stored examples are the R-0.5 arcs: {8: 7.5, 16: 15.5, 24: 23.5, 32: 31.5} (verified by executing the loop). _sections_fig then titles each panel 'Arc transect at radius {R} km' with the dict key, so arcB_sections.png shows the 7.5/15.5/23.5/31.5 km cross-sections labeled as 8/16/24/32 km.
failure_scenario: Run build_arc_B.py as-is: outputs/arcB_sections.png panel 1 plots the 7.5 km arc (its channels, floodplain ref, bed, crest) under the title 'Arc transect at radius 8 km from anchor'. Anyone cross-referencing the figure against arcB_channels.parquet rows at R_km=8.0 compares two different transects 500 m apart.
suggested_fix: Capture on exact match: `if R in example_R` with example_R = [8.0, 16.0, 24.0, 32.0], or label the panel with the actual R used.

title: Headline superelevation silently falls back from SWOT-median stage to DEM stage per-radius, mixing stage bases that differ by up to 1.3 m
description: `ch['kan_superelev_m'] = ch['kan_superelev_med_m'].fillna(ch['kan_superelev_dem_m'])` (and the Uyak twin) splices two quantities with different stage definitions into one unflagged column: the SWOT-median-stage superelevation and the DEM-mosaic-stage superelevation. On the committed data these differ per-arc by -1.30 to +1.01 m (Kanektok) and -0.78 to +0.69 m (Uyak) where both exist. Today the fallback fires on 0 rows (only R=3.0 lacks the SWOT median, and fp_ref is also NaN there), but the guard is MIN_PASSES=8 per (river, radius) in swot_arc_reference.py — any rebuild with thinner coverage (e.g. from the smaller swot_apr_jul_2025_2026.parquet candidate, or extended radii) silently produces a superelevation-vs-radius curve whose level jumps by up to ~1 m at the radii where the source switches, with no flag column distinguishing the two regimes.
failure_scenario: Rebuild swot_arc_reference.parquet from a SWOT source where some radius has <8 Kanektok passes (the second listed candidate, or a future radius extension): at that radius kan_superelev_m becomes the DEM-stage value while neighbours stay SWOT-median-stage; the dashboard Cross-Sections tab renders a step of up to ~1.3 m in the 'primary' superelevation curve that is pure stage artifact, indistinguishable from a real perching signal.
suggested_fix: Add a boolean source flag column (e.g. kan_superelev_src = 'swot_med'|'dem'), or drop the fallback and leave NaN so the plotted curve gaps instead of switching stage basis.

title: Snap-window 'clipped' QC flag can miss wall-limited picks because the center is the median of the deepest-percentile points
description: The wall flag is `abs(k_off) >= SNAP_WIN_KAN_M - ARC_STEP_M` (>= 73 m), but the reported center is not an extreme sample: it is `np.median(arc_m[search & (z <= thr)])` over the deepest-P2 points (comment says 'centroid', code is median). Re-running the snap on the real raster: the deepest-percentile selection is typically 2 points (median count 2) with positional spread up to 74 m, so when the deepest terrain is truncated by the +/-75 m wall, the median can sit well inside the wall (e.g. one point at the wall, one 40 m inside -> offset ~55 m) and the pick evades the clipped flag while still being wall-limited. Also, the actual linspace sample spacing is arc_len/(n-1) > 2.0 m, so the threshold win - ARC_STEP_M is marginally too high for a pick at the last in-window sample. In the committed data 6 Kanektok / 5 Uyak arcs are flagged and offsets reach 73.9 m, so the flag mostly works; the failure mode is under-reporting in the migration QC, not a wrong WSE (measured WSE is insensitive, and one arc, R=33.5, already has its median-center 52 m from the window argmin).
failure_scenario: An arc where the DEM channel migrated beyond the +/-75 m window but a secondary low sits 40 m inside it: the P2 selection straddles both, the median lands ~35-55 m from the prior, kan_snap_clipped stays False, and the 'AT THE WALL on N% of arcs' QC statistic understates how many crest windows are anchored on a lower-bound position.
suggested_fix: Flag when the search window itself was truncated (lo/hi hit the wall AND any selected deep point lies within one sample spacing of the wall), rather than thresholding the median offset.

title: Shared spherical/haversine radial coordinate understates true ground distance by ~0.36%, inflating all per-km gradients by the same factor
description: dest()/dist_bear() (R=6371.0088) and SWOT_Pull/DEM_Pull haversine (R=6371.0) are mutually consistent — a DEM arc point at nominal R has archive-convention dist_km exactly R (verified: 0.0 m mismatch at all tested radii/bearings) — but the spherical convention compresses real WGS84 distances at this latitude: a point truly 34.5 km from the anchor (pyproj Geod, WGS84) gets dist_km = 34.375 km (-0.36%). The spherical destination also sits 10-125 m from the true geodesic destination over 3-34.5 km. Because the shortfall is a uniform scale factor applied identically to both rivers and to both SWOT and DEM, all comparative conclusions (Uyak-Kanektok, beta, superelevation) are unaffected; but absolute per-km numbers quoted in the thesis (e.g. canonical gradients 195.4 / 191.7 cm/km) are systematically ~0.36% high (~0.7 cm/km) because the denominator km is short.
failure_scenario: Quoting 'Kanektok gradient 195.4 cm/km' as a physical slope: the true along-radial slope is ~194.7 cm/km. Any external comparison against a slope computed with proper geodesic or projected distances carries a built-in 0.36% offset.
suggested_fix: Either document the spherical-distance convention where gradients are quoted, or switch dist_km/dest to pyproj.Geod (WGS84) everywhere at once — never in only one component, since the current correctness rests on every component using the same sphere.

title: swot_arc_reference builds the 'archive' stats from dashboard_data.parquet (60 open-water passes), not the full 188-pass archive its docstring claims
description: The docstring says the script 'Condenses the full SWOT pixel archive', but SWOT_CANDIDATES prefers ROOT/dashboard_data.parquet, which contains 60 passes (2.4M rows, Apr-Jul open-water seasons 2023-2026), while batch_outputs/master_all_data_part_*.parquet holds 188 passes (7.9M rows) including winter. Excluding ice-season passes is almost certainly the right science, but it is an undocumented consequence of which file happens to sit in ROOT: the published 'stage distribution' (median/p10/p90 per radius) and diff_pass_paired stats are open-water-season statistics, and they silently change if dashboard_data.parquet is swapped for a different release subset. The 'median stage' the thesis superelevation is quoted at is the Apr-Jul median, not an annual one.
failure_scenario: A future rebuild after dashboard_data.parquet is regenerated with a different date range (the file has already grown from the documented 29 passes to 60) silently shifts swot_*_wse_med_m and hence every headline superelevation value, with no provenance recorded in the output parquet.
suggested_fix: State the open-water-season restriction in the docstring, and write the source filename + pass count/date range into the parquet (or print-log them) so the reference artifact carries its provenance.

title: beta_floodplain.py depends on unversioned /tmp inputs that no longer exist, so the published beta reproduction cannot be re-run
description: GDB = '/tmp/clean_and_complete.gdb' and the validation overlay path '/tmp/original_beta.parquet' point at volatile /tmp locations; neither exists now (verified). The script that produced the beta_floodplain.parquet numbers and the rebuild-vs-original validation figure is therefore not reproducible from the repository — gpd.read_file raises immediately. The hardcoded x-axis in the validation overlay (ox = arange(len(o)) * (26.68/len(o))) also assumes a fixed transect count/extent that is only implicit.
failure_scenario: Anyone (including the author after a reboot clears /tmp) running `python3 DEM_Transects/beta_floodplain.py` to regenerate or check the thesis beta numbers gets a DriverError: '/tmp/clean_and_complete.gdb' does not exist, and the recovered-ArcGIS comparison cannot be reproduced.
suggested_fix: Move the recovered gdb (or an exported GeoPackage of Avulsion_Lines_2 / Guide_Lines_2) and original_beta.parquet into DEM_Transects/data or DEM_Transects/reference and point the constants there.

title: DEM_Pull assumes river_poly.zip is EPSG:4326 without reprojecting
description: main() reads the polygon and uses gdf.total_bounds directly as degree coordinates for the ee.Geometry.Rectangle, and sample_dem_within_polygons masks the EPSG:4326 raster with row.geometry, with no .to_crs() anywhere. It works only because river_poly.zip happens to be EPSG:4326 (verified). DEM_2m_Pull.py handles the same file correctly (g3413 = gdf.to_crs(MOSAIC_CRS)). If the polygon file is ever re-exported from ArcGIS in EPSG:3413 (like every other layer in this project), the GEE region becomes a degenerate rectangle in meter-coordinates interpreted as degrees and rio_mask returns empty/garbage rather than an obvious CRS error.
failure_scenario: Replace river_poly.zip with a 3413-projected export: export_dem_from_gee builds a Rectangle at e.g. lon=-2998526 which GEE rejects or wraps, and if the old tif exists the masking step silently yields 'no valid pixels' for both rivers.
suggested_fix: Add gdf = gdf.to_crs(4326) after reading, mirroring DEM_2m_Pull.py.

title: Thesis labels Uyak seasonal slope p=0.033 as 'Not Significant'; pipeline reports it significant
description: temporal_analysis.py:_mwu (line 143) labels any p<0.05 'significant', and the archived run produced p=0.0327 for the Uyak pooled seasonal slope contrast (temporal_results/temporal_analysis_results.json: Q1_slope_pooled, Uyak_Creek, p_slope=0.0327, n_high=10, n_low=15). The script therefore printed '-> seasonal slope swing +2.3 cm/km [p=0.033 (significant, n=10 vs 15)]', and the dashboard's _fmt_p (dashboard_swot.py:3483) renders it '0.033 *' (starred as significant). But the thesis table (Project_Info/'Masters Thesis (6).pdf', seasonal-slope table) prints 'Not Significant (p=0.033)' for exactly this comparison — a direct contradiction of the pipeline's own stated alpha=0.05 convention, in a published table. TEMPORAL_ANALYSIS.md:101 calls the same result 'marginally so'. Three artifacts, three different verdicts for one number.
failure_scenario: Ran pdftotext on Project_Info/'Masters Thesis (6).pdf' and grepped: the table row reads 'Uyak | 193.5 cm/km | 191.2 cm/km | +2.3 cm/km | Not Significant (p=0.033)'. Reproduced the script's output path: p=0.0327 -> line 143 assigns 'significant'. A committee member checking the table against alpha=0.05 (or against the live dashboard, which stars it) sees the thesis asserting the opposite of its own analysis code.
suggested_fix: Either correct the thesis label to 'significant (p=0.033)' with the existing caveat that the effect is small and year-inconsistent, or explicitly justify 'not significant' via a multiple-comparison correction (with ~14 MWU tests, Bonferroni alpha ~0.0036 would make it n.s.) and state that correction in both the thesis and TEMPORAL_ANALYSIS.md; make _mwu/_fmt_p and the thesis use the same rule.

title: Date-keyed checkpoints keep only the FIRST granule per calendar day: second same-day passes and same-pass sibling tiles are silently discarded
description: Daily CSVs are keyed by date only (is_date_already_processed, lines 183-186; skip at 585-588). process_granule writes {date}_data.csv after the first granule that yields data, so every subsequent granule with the same date — including sibling tiles of the SAME pass and granules of a genuinely DIFFERENT overpass later that day — is skipped forever. CMR query (SWOT_L2_HR_PIXC_D, AOI bbox, 2023-07..2026-08) returns 998 granules on 294 dates; 272 dates have >1 granule and 59 dates have TWO DISTINCT passes (e.g. 2023-08-21 has pass 293 at 13:24 and pass 304 at 22:15). 56 of those two-pass dates are in the archive, whose code guarantees at most one granule per date, so ~56 independent overpasses are absent from the record. Tile-boundary loss is also visible: all 50 archived pass-571 days contain only a 4.3 km upstream Kanektok fragment (dist 30.7-35.1 km, lat<=59.766) and a 0.18 km Uyak sliver, cut on a straight line at lat~59.77 (an along-track tile boundary), while CMR shows same-day sibling tiles (e.g. 2024-05-07 260L: box lat 59.05-59.87, lon -162.74..-161.15; 261L) whose footprints enclose the rest of both rivers.
failure_scenario: Ran CMR queries + DuckDB against batch_outputs/master_all_data_part_*.parquet: Kanektok span by same-day granule count shows the n_gran=4 group (pass 571 days) at median span 4.34 km vs 34.75 km for other passes; Uyak median 0.18 km. Example 2024-05-07: archive holds only dist 30.8-35.1 km of Kanektok from one tile while granule 014_571_260L (covering the full river extent) was skipped because 2024-05-07_data.csv already existed. Net effect: the 'full archive' underlying the thesis pass counts, elevation-difference pairing, fine-scale slope and temporal analysis is missing ~56 whole overpasses plus the majority of every pass-571 acquisition. (Headline gated reference-gradient medians survive because the fragments fail the span/start gate, but sample sizes and coverage claims are understated, and the loss is silent and unrecoverable without a re-pull.)
suggested_fix: Key checkpoints by granule ID (or date+pass+tile), e.g. one CSV per granule or append-with-dedupe into the daily CSV; then re-pull the archive. At minimum log a loud warning when a granule is skipped because its date-file exists but the granule ID was never processed.

title: MAD outlier filter on raw WSE amputates the upstream half of Uyak Creek on 28% of dates and misses real outliers
description: `calculate_mad_outliers` (line 121) is applied to RAW per-reach WSE (line 316-320), not to residuals from the along-river trend. The reach has ~66 m of real relief over 35 km, so median/MAD are dominated by the trend and by the pixel-density distribution along the profile. Two failure modes, both demonstrated on real archive data: (a) When density is downstream-weighted (narrow upstream creek, wide lower river — typical for Uyak), the median sits near the low downstream WSE, MAD is small, and the band `median ± 5.19*MAD` classifies ALL legitimate upstream water as outliers, deleting entire river reaches. (b) When density is uniform (Kanektok), MAD ≈ 14 m, the band is ±73 m, and genuine multi-meter outliers pass untouched. The `MIN_POINTS_AFTER_FILTER=5` safety check (line 324) permits removing thousands of points as long as 5 survive. Effect on published numbers: 46 of 167 dates with both rivers have Uyak's coverage start >1 km behind Kanektok's on the identical repeating orbit; 7 of the 67 gated open-water Uyak passes feeding the canonical reference gradient are amputated at 1-3 km (inside the REFGRAD_MAX_START_KM=3.0 gate), and their median |Theil-Sen slope| is 184.6 cm/km vs 192.0 for the 60 clean passes — i.e., the exact steep-reach-clipping bias the coverage gate was designed to exclude, depressing the published Uyak 191.7 cm/km. The amputation is spread across all months, so it also contaminates the seasonal/temporal analysis and the Kanektok-vs-Uyak gated-pass-count asymmetry (88 vs 67).
failure_scenario: Ran on 2023-09-01 (pass 026) Uyak, n=17,660 stored (already once-filtered) points: raw-domain MAD = 2.13 m -> band -6.6..15.5 m -> re-applying the exact repo function removes another 4,340 points (25%), 100% of every node from 13-22 km (wse 15.5-35.5 m), while residual-domain MAD (Theil-Sen detrend) removes 0. Same date Kanektok: raw MAD band ±72.8 m removes 0 points while residual-domain finds 178 outliers up to 11.8 m off-trend. Archive-wide fingerprint across the 45 repeats of identical pass 026: Uyak coverage start jumps between 0.31 and 25.26 km date-to-date with wse_max clipped in lockstep (e.g., 2023-11-03: starts 20.0 km, wse_max 19.15 m, 201-413 px at the first surviving nodes and zero above, while Kanektok has 660-780 px per node in the same swath region — the region was imaged; only a WSE-thresholding step can cut at a wse isoline, and MAD is the only such step in the pipeline).
suggested_fix: Detrend first: fit a robust along-distance trend (Theil-Sen on 1-km node medians, same model as compute_reference_gradient) per reach-pass, then apply the modified-z MAD test to residuals. Also cap the fraction removable (e.g., skip if >10% flagged) instead of the 5-point floor. Re-pull or re-filter from raw granules — the daily CSVs are post-amputation, so the deleted points are not recoverable from checkpoints.

title: astype(int) on geolocation_qual crashes the whole granule if the column is partially NaN
description: Line 292 guards with df_exact['geolocation_qual'].notna().any() (ANY, not ALL), then line 293 does .astype(int) on the float column. If even one pixel decodes as NaN (xarray converts _FillValue in the uint32 flag to NaN), pandas raises ValueError('Cannot convert non-finite values (NA or inf) to integer'). The raise is swallowed by the broad except at line 359, which prints one 'Failed' line and returns None — so the ENTIRE granule (all reaches, all pixels) is dropped, no daily CSV is written, and every future resumable run retries and fails identically, leaving a permanent silent hole in the archive.
failure_scenario: pd.Series([64.0, np.nan]).astype(int) -> ValueError (verified behavior). A PIXC granule with one fill-valued geolocation_qual pixel inside the AOI: cross-track filter passes, line 293 raises, tqdm.write prints '❌ <date>: Failed - Cannot convert non-finite values...' among hundreds of progress lines, and that pass is absent from the master with no flag anywhere. Cannot confirm an occurrence in the current archive (qual columns are not exported to the daily CSVs), but the crash path is deterministic given a single NaN.
suggested_fix: Treat NaN qual as its own category: mask = df_exact['geolocation_qual'].fillna(0).astype('int64') & XOVERCAL_MISSING_MASK == 0 (or drop NaN-qual pixels explicitly), and narrow the except so ingestion errors are counted/reported per granule.

title: Checkpoint staleness: filter-constant changes never propagate; rebuild re-applies only KNOWN_BAD_PASSES and column pruning
description: Verified what rebuild_master_from_daily_csvs (457-556) does: concat daily CSVs, drop KNOWN_BAD_PASSES rows (488-495), prune to KEEP_COLUMNS, dtype-optimize, write master + partitions, recompute reference gradient. It re-applies NO science filters — and it cannot: cross_track, geolocation_qual and classification_qual are deliberately not exported to the daily CSVs (cols_export, line 350), so a change to CROSS_TRACK_MIN/MAX, XOVERCAL masks, MAD_THRESHOLD or DEFAULT_CLASSES requires a full re-download, while is_date_already_processed (183-186) makes a re-run silently skip every existing date. A researcher editing a filter constant and re-running gets an unchanged master with no warning. Currently benign in effect: all 189 daily CSVs have mtime 2026-07-14, after the last filter change (crossover filter, commit d22d66d 2026-04-01), and classification in the CSVs is uniformly {3,4} — so today's archive is consistent; the defect is the unguarded process.
failure_scenario: Tomorrow the user re-enables the disabled bit-flag filters per the TODO at lines 298-303 and runs SWOT_Pull.py over the same date range: every granule is skipped ('already processed'), rebuild regenerates the master from the OLD unfiltered CSVs, and the reference gradient is republished as if the new filter had been applied.
suggested_fix: Stamp each daily CSV (or a sidecar manifest) with a hash of the filter configuration; at rebuild, warn or refuse when CSV stamps mismatch the current constants. Alternatively export the qual columns so rebuild can re-filter.

title: ~14 uncorrected Mann-Whitney tests and an uncertainty-free point-median Q3 verdict
description: The run performs 16 MWU tests (Q1 pooled slope x2, Q1 WSE per year x6 of which 2 return NaN for n<3, Q2 x4, Q3 x4 — 14 with valid p), each judged at raw alpha=0.05 in _mwu (line 143) with no family-wise correction, and results are exported to JSON/dashboard/thesis. Separately, the Q3 'exceeds/within natural baseline' verdict (lines 277-279) is a bare comparison of two point medians, abs(dwse) > abs(baseline_dwse), computed from n=4 vs ~4 June passes, with no CI/bootstrap — a sign flip in either small-sample median flips the published verdict. Note the interaction with the thesis finding above: the only raw-significant temporal result (Uyak p=0.033) would be n.s. under any family-wise correction, but no such correction is stated anywhere.
failure_scenario: With 14 tests at alpha=0.05 the expected false-positive count under the global null is ~0.7; the single p=0.033 hit is exactly the pattern multiplicity produces, yet the JSON/dashboard star it as significant while the thesis (without stating a correction) calls it not significant. For Q3: temporal_analysis_results.json Q3_typhoon rows carry 'wse_vs_baseline' verdicts derived from medians of 3-4 passes; moving one 2026 June pass by ~0.1 m flips 'within' to 'exceeds'.
suggested_fix: Report Holm/Bonferroni-adjusted p-values (or FDR) in the JSON and docs, and replace the Q3 verdict with a bootstrap CI on the median difference (or at least report the IQRs already computed and phrase the verdict conditionally).

title: Duplicate QC exclusion registries: SWOT_Pull.KNOWN_BAD_PASSES vs thesis_figures/config.EXCLUDED_PASSES
description: The same scientific exclusion ('2025-04-17' ice pass) is maintained in two hand-synced dicts: SWOT_Pull.py:70 KNOWN_BAD_PASSES (filters the master/reference gradient at rebuild) and thesis_figures/config.py:66 EXCLUDED_PASSES (filters every thesis-figure data path via core._exclusion_condition/_drop_excluded). SWOT_Pull.py:69 even documents 'Kept in sync with thesis_figures/config.EXCLUDED_PASSES' — an instruction to a human, not a mechanism. They currently match (verified: both contain exactly 2025-04-17), but the failure mode is one-sided: a pass added only to KNOWN_BAD_PASSES disappears from the master (figures consistent by luck), while a pass added only to EXCLUDED_PASSES leaves the master, dashboard and temporal_analysis.py (which reads master parts directly and has NO registry of its own) including data the thesis figures exclude — silently divergent published numbers.
failure_scenario: Next ice-contaminated pass is spotted while making figures and added to config.EXCLUDED_PASSES only: thesis Figs exclude it, but the dashboard headline gradient, reference_gradient_per_pass.parquet and temporal_results/*.json still include it; thesis text quoting the dashboard numbers no longer matches its own figures.
suggested_fix: Single source: a small JSON/py module at repo root (e.g. qc_exclusions.py) imported by SWOT_Pull.py and thesis_figures/config.py (dashboard inherits via the master); assert equality in a test if import coupling is undesirable.

title: Superseded density-biased per-pass pixel OLS (slope_calc) still computed and exported; understates both gradients and doubles the inter-river contrast
description: Lines 343-347 still fit stats.linregress on RAW PIXELS per reach per granule and export it as slope_calc in every daily CSV and the master, even though the project's verified reference gradient (node-median Theil-Sen, compute_reference_gradient) explicitly superseded it as density-biased. Quantified against the real archive (merge of master slope_calc with reference_gradient_per_pass.parquet, 276 passes): gated passes diverge by median -6.5 cm/km (|delta| p90 16.4, max 25.7); ungated median -12.8, max 40.9 (worst: Uyak 2025-12-03, -133.8 vs -174.8). Headline medians recomputed from slope_calc would be Kanektok 190.5 / Uyak 184.2 instead of the published 195.4 / 191.7 — and the Kanektok-minus-Uyak advantage, the thesis's core avulsion metric, would read 6.3 cm/km instead of 3.7 (nearly double). The dashboard still queries it (MEDIAN(slope_calc) -> avg_slope, dashboard_swot.py:1395-1401) though avg_slope is currently not displayed; the column also surfaces in the Raw Data tab and CSV exports with no 'superseded' marking.
failure_scenario: A collaborator (or the user in a hurry) computes a river gradient from the distributed master parquet's slope_calc column — the obvious-looking field — and reports a 6.3 cm/km inter-river contrast, 70% larger than the validated 3.7 cm/km, with per-pass errors up to ~26 cm/km on gated passes.
suggested_fix: Either drop slope_calc from KEEP_COLUMNS/cols_export (reference_gradient_per_pass.parquet is the sanctioned per-pass slope), or rename it (e.g. slope_pixel_ols_deprecated) and delete the dead avg_slope leg of the dashboard stats query.

title: core.py retains savgol/gaussian fine-slope estimators deleted from the dashboard, under a 'Ported VERBATIM' contract
description: thesis_figures/core.py:211-216 states the fine-scale block is 'Ported VERBATIM from dashboard_swot.py's compute_finescale_slope + _fine_slope_*', and _FINE_ESTIMATORS (255-259) offers theilsen/savgol/gaussian. The dashboard now contains only _fine_slope_theilsen (dashboard_swot.py:320; hardcoded fn at 398) — savgol and gaussian were deleted there. The module's own header (core.py:8-9) declares divergence from the dashboard a bug. Currently harmless in outputs: the only caller, make_figures.py:875 build_fig9, defaults to method='theilsen'. But the retained estimators are an untested drift surface that the module contract explicitly forbids, and a caller passing method='gaussian' would produce a figure reproducing nothing in the validated dashboard.
failure_scenario: A future figure is built with method='savgol' (offered by the API and documented as dashboard-verbatim); its slope profile differs from the dashboard's theilsen tab, violating the figures-match-dashboard guarantee the thesis methods section relies on.
suggested_fix: Delete _fine_slope_savgol, _fine_slope_gaussian and the _FINE_ESTIMATORS dict (keep theilsen inline), or update the docstring to say they are retained for method-comparison only and are NOT dashboard-matched.

title: Silent load_tide=0 fallback with no warning or flag column (currently never triggered)
description: Lines 246-247: if neither load_tide_fes nor load_tide_height exists in a granule, load_tide is silently set to scalar 0 and WSE (line 262) simply omits that correction, with no warning, no flag column, and no way to distinguish 'correction genuinely ~0' from 'correction missing' downstream except an exact-zero test. Verified against the full archive: 0 of 7,895,912 rows have load_tide == 0 exactly (range -0.036..+0.028 m, mean |.| 1.0 cm), so the fallback has never fired on real data and no published number is affected — the suspicion holds as a latent hazard only. If a future PIXC version renames the variable, every new pass would carry a systematic ~+/-1-3.5 cm WSE bias, comparable to the seasonal WSE signals (0.2-0.5 m) being resolved at the cm level.
failure_scenario: A PIXC version E renames load_tide_fes: all new granules ingest with load_tide=0, WSE shifts ~1-3 cm relative to the older record, and the temporal analysis interprets the step as an interannual water-level change. Nothing in logs or outputs flags the substitution.
suggested_fix: tqdm.write a per-granule warning and/or set load_tide to NaN (failing loudly downstream) instead of 0; optionally add a boolean load_tide_missing column.

title: Cross-track filter silently skipped when the variable is absent/all-NaN
description: Line 281: the 10-60 km cross-track gate runs only if the column exists and has any non-NaN value; otherwise the granule proceeds unfiltered (nadir-gap and far-swath pixels retained) with no message — the skip is indistinguishable from a pass. Confirmed the code path; assessed impact as latent: cross_track is a core PIXC variable present in all Version-D granules, the column is unconditionally created (line 252) so the 'in columns' clause is always true, and the daily CSVs don't export it so an occurrence can't be audited after the fact. No evidence any archived pass was ingested unfiltered. Note the mirror behavior is silently strict: pixels whose cross_track is NaN while others are valid are dropped by the >= comparison without being counted in the log line.
failure_scenario: A malformed/renamed cross_track in a future product version: every pixel including <10 km nadir-gap geolocations enters the WSE record for that granule, degrading its slope, and the only trace is the ABSENCE of one 'Quality Filter: ... cross_track' log line in a scrolling tqdm session.
suggested_fix: Invert the guard: if cross_track is missing/all-NaN, tqdm.write an explicit WARNING (or reject the granule), since the filter is a documented part of the method.

title: XOVERCAL_SUSPECT_MASK defined but never applied; height_cor_xover_qual extracted but never used
description: Confirmed by exhaustive grep: XOVERCAL_SUSPECT_MASK (line 28, bit 6 'crossover calibration suspect') appears nowhere else in the repo — only the MISSING mask (bit 23) is applied at line 293. height_cor_xover_qual is extracted per pixel at line 253, then never referenced: not filtered on, not in cols_export (350) nor KEEP_COLUMNS. Suspicion holds exactly as stated. Impact is limited to (a) dead memory/IO work per granule and (b) a misleading signal that suspect-flagged crossover-cal pixels are being screened when they are not — pixels with bit 6 set (suspect calibration) are retained in the science record. Whether that retention matters is undetermined (the suspect rate over this AOI is unknown; the disabled-filters note at 298-303 suggests conservative filtering was deliberate).
failure_scenario: A methods reader (or reviewer) sees both masks defined under 'Crossover calibration quality filter' constants and reasonably concludes suspect pixels are excluded; they are not, and no output allows checking how many suspect pixels are in the record since the qual column is discarded.
suggested_fix: Either apply the suspect mask (or log its would-be hit rate per granule), or delete the constant and the height_cor_xover_qual extraction and note in SCIENTIFIC_METHODOLOGY.md that only bit 23 is screened.

title: len(df_final) > 5 silently drops small valid reach/pass point sets (and is off-by-one with MIN_POINTS_AFTER_FILTER)
description: Line 336 appends a reach's points only if len(df_final) > 5, so a reach imaged with 1-5 valid pixels on a pass is silently absent from the daily CSV/master — no log line (unlike every other filter). Also internally inconsistent: MIN_POINTS_AFTER_FILTER = 5 (line 34, 'ensure statistical validity') deliberately allows exactly 5 points to survive MAD, which line 336 then discards. Impact on published numbers is nil in practice: 5 pixels cannot form >=8 one-km nodes, so such sets could never enter the reference gradient or temporal metrics; the loss is archival completeness (e.g. a 5-pixel Uyak sliver on a fragment day) and provenance, not bias. Suspicion confirmed but benign for the science.
failure_scenario: A pass images Uyak with 5 valid pixels after filtering; the MAD block logs nothing and line 336 drops them; the daily CSV shows Kanektok only, and a coverage audit undercounts Uyak observations with no trace of why.
suggested_fix: Use >= MIN_POINTS_AFTER_FILTER (one constant, one meaning) and tqdm.write a 'dropped small set (n=...)' line for symmetry with the other filters.

title: Global warnings.filterwarnings('ignore') suppresses all warnings in the ingestion pipeline
description: Line 91 blanket-suppresses every warning process-wide in the scientific ingestion script: scipy linregress/theilslopes degenerate-input RuntimeWarnings, numpy invalid-value warnings, xarray decode warnings (e.g. unrecognized _FillValue handling that would foreshadow the geolocation_qual NaN crash), pandas dtype fallbacks, and geopandas CRS warnings. Confirmed present and unconditional. No current published number is shown to be wrong because of it, but it is precisely the class of signal that would have surfaced the other latent defects here (NaN qual flags, missing tide variable) at ingestion time.
failure_scenario: xarray emits a SerializationWarning while decoding a malformed granule (fill values left undecoded); it is suppressed; the granule ingests with fill-valued heights that MAD partially passes, and the first visible symptom is an anomalous pass in a thesis figure months later.
suggested_fix: Remove the global ignore, or scope it to the specific known-noisy categories (e.g. warnings.filterwarnings('ignore', category=FutureWarning, module='geopandas')) and let RuntimeWarnings print.

title: Stale hardcoded shoulder-month statistics in OPEN_WATER_MONTHS comment (37/136 vs current 37/155)
description: The comment at lines 59-66 justifies keeping April/November with 'the shoulder months (Apr, Nov) supply 37/136 = 27% of gated open-water passes' plus per-month slope values from the 2026-07 validation. Verified against the current artifacts: temporal_results/temporal_metrics_per_pass.parquet now has 155 gated open-water passes of which 37 are Apr/Nov = 24%, and temporal_analysis_results.json records n_full_coverage_open_water=155. The 37/136 snapshot is stale (denominator grew with the archive) and will drift further with every pull; the qualitative justification still holds, so this is a documentation-accuracy issue only. Suspicion confirmed as stated, impact benign.
failure_scenario: The thesis methods section cites the in-code justification '27% of 136 passes' while the results section reports 155 passes; a careful reviewer flags the internal inconsistency.
suggested_fix: Replace the hardcoded counts with a dated 'validated 2026-07 on the then-current archive (37/136)' phrasing, or compute and print the shoulder share at runtime instead of embedding it in a comment.

title: TYPHOON_DATE constant does not drive the analysis; June comparison windows are hardcoded independently
description: TYPHOON_DATE ('2025-10-12', line 71) is referenced exactly once — echoed into the JSON 'method' block (line 381) — so it is metadata, not a parameter. The actual pre/post windows are hardcoded elsewhere: q3_typhoon uses _period(df, reach, 2025, {6}) / _period(df, reach, 2026, {6}) (lines 259-260) and q3_profile uses literal '2025-06-01'..'2026-06-30' (lines 330-331). Confirmed exactly as suspected. The constant creates a false affordance: editing it (e.g. to re-anchor on a corrected landfall date or a new storm) changes nothing except the JSON metadata, which would then MIS-DESCRIBE the frozen June windows.
failure_scenario: A second storm in 2027 prompts changing TYPHOON_DATE to rerun the Q3 machinery; the script still compares June 2025 vs June 2026, but the exported JSON now claims the new typhoon_date — dashboard and write-up captions inherit the wrong provenance.
suggested_fix: Derive the windows from the constant (pre = last matched open-water month before it, post = same month next year) or demote it to a documented string in the summary dict with a comment that windows are hardcoded at 259-260/330-331.

title: Stale docstring: core.elevation_difference claims to 'improve on the dashboard's pooled AVG', but the dashboard already uses the same per-pass paired method
description: core.py:356 says the method 'improves on the dashboard's pooled AVG, which is artifact-sensitive'. Verified against dashboard_swot.py:2224-2260: the dashboard's Elevation Difference tab now computes exactly the same per-(pass,bin) median, both-rivers-paired, median-across-passes difference (its comment even says 'Replaces the older pooled-AVG difference'). The docstring describes a dashboard that no longer exists, inverting the module's lockstep contract (header lines 8-9): a reader would conclude figure and dashboard use DIFFERENT methods when they are intentionally identical. No numeric impact; classic drift-surface documentation bug in a module whose stated invariant is dashboard parity.
failure_scenario: The thesis methods chapter, written from core.py docstrings, states the figures use a superior method to the public dashboard; a committee member cross-checks the live dashboard and finds the identical method, undermining confidence in the methods text.
suggested_fix: Rewrite the docstring: 'Same per-pass paired-median method as the dashboard's Elevation Difference tab (which replaced the older pooled AVG in <commit/date>).'

title: KNOWN_BAD_PASSES exclusion rationale hardcodes gradient medians that will go stale as the archive grows
description: The 2025-04-17 exclusion reason (lines 71-75, duplicated in thesis_figures/config.py:67-72) embeds 'Uyak 236, Kanektok 224 cm/km vs medians 192/196'. Today those medians are still approximately right (canonical gated open-water medians verified in this review: Kanektok 195.4, Uyak 191.7 — the string's 196/192 rounds to them), so the suspicion of present staleness does NOT hold; the defect is prospective: the medians are recomputed on every pull (compute_reference_gradient) while the string is frozen, and this reason text is printed into rebuild logs (line 494) and serves as the documented QC evidence. The anomalous per-pass values (236/224) are legitimately frozen facts; the comparison baseline is not.
failure_scenario: After two more seasons the recomputed medians drift to, say, 194/190; the exclusion registry still asserts 192/196 as 'the medians', and the QC documentation quoted in the thesis appendix no longer matches reference_gradient_per_pass.parquet.
suggested_fix: Phrase the baseline as dated evidence ('vs medians 192/196 as of the 2026-07 archive') in BOTH registry copies, or store only the frozen anomalous values and compare against live medians at print time.

title: Date-keyed checkpoint silently drops 169 co-dated granules; pass 571 loses ~85% of the river profile on 50 dates
description: Checkpoints are keyed by calendar date only (`is_date_already_processed` checks `{date}_data.csv`, line 183-186; the CSV is written per-granule at line 352). SWOT PIXC granules are per-TILE, and one pass over these rivers regularly produces two tiles on the same date. After the first tile writes the CSV, every later granule of that date is skipped forever at line 585 — and because the CSV now exists, the lost tiles can never be ingested by a resume run. NASA CMR shows 421 SWOT_L2_HR_PIXC_D granules intersecting the study bbox (2023-07 to 2026-08) across 252 dates, 151 dates with >1 granule: 169 granules are never processed. Tile pairs per pass: 293 -> 261R+261L, 332 -> 048L+049L, 571 -> 260L+261L. For pass 571 the first-sorted tile (260L) covers only the distal end: all 50 processed 571-dates contain Kanektok only from dist_km 30.7-35.1 (vs 0.3-35.1 on every other pass) and Uyak is absent on 22 dates / ~38 points at km 35.2 on the other 28 — while the skipped 261L tile's CMR footprint covers 100% of both river polygons. Roughly a quarter of the archive's dates are near-empty observations that downstream products (master parquet, dashboard, temporal_analysis, per-pass counts in reference_gradient_per_pass.parquet: Kanektok n=88 vs Uyak n=67 gated open-water) treat as the complete pass.
failure_scenario: Ran: CMR granule query for the polygon bbox -> 421 granules / 252 dates vs 189 daily CSVs on disk; grouped granules per date -> 169 skipped, 0 dates with two distinct passes (all collisions are same-pass tiles). Loaded all daily CSVs grouped by pass: pass 571 (50 dates) has Kanektok dist_km 30.72-35.06 median coverage and Uyak median n=38 points, vs full 0.31-35.06 coverage for passes 026/293/332. Tile 261L (54 granules, bbox 59.59-60.40N covering 100% of both river polygons) never appears in any output. Concrete failure: the 2023-08-31 run downloads 571_260L, writes 2023-08-31_data.csv with only the distal stub, then skips 571_261L at line 585; every subsequent resume run skips it too.
suggested_fix: Key checkpoints by granule (e.g., `{date}_{pass}_{tile}_data.csv` from the granule name) and have the rebuild concatenate all files per date; or accumulate/merge multiple granules per date before writing the daily CSV. Then delete the 50 truncated pass-571 CSVs (and 293/332 dates if the second tile adds pixels) and re-pull.

title: geolocation_qual.astype(int) crashes on partially-NaN flag column, silently discarding the whole granule
description: xarray decodes _FillValue pixels of geolocation_qual to NaN (float column). The guard `df_exact['geolocation_qual'].notna().any()` (line 292) enters the filter branch when ANY value is valid, but `.astype(int)` on line 293 raises `IntCastingNaNError` if ANY value is NaN. So a granule where even one in-polygon pixel has fill geolocation_qual (mixed with valid pixels) throws, is caught by the catch-all `except` at line 359, prints one scrolling '❌ Failed' line, and returns None — the entire granule (all reaches, all tiles that date) is dropped from the archive. Because no CSV is written, every future resume run re-downloads and re-fails identically: a permanent, effectively silent hole in the record. The guard's existence shows partial-NaN was anticipated; the cast defeats it.
failure_scenario: Constructed and ran the exact failing case under the environment's pandas 2.3.2: `s = pd.Series([3.0, np.nan, 8388608.0]); s.notna().any() -> True; (s.astype(int) & 8388608)` raises `IntCastingNaNError: Cannot convert non-finite values (NA or inf) to integer`. In process_granule this propagates to the outer except -> granule skipped with only a tqdm line; main() counts it neither as processed nor as failed in the summary (line 596).
suggested_fix: Treat NaN qual as its own category, e.g. `q = df_exact['geolocation_qual']; xover_mask = q.notna() & (q.fillna(0).astype('int64') & XOVERCAL_MISSING_MASK == 0)` (or keep NaN-qual pixels explicitly if that is the intended policy). Same latent pattern applies to any future use of classification_qual/height_cor_xover_qual.

title: Exported slope_calc is a density-biased pixel OLS, fit to tile-truncated and MAD-amputated profiles
description: slope_calc (lines 343-347) is an OLS fit over raw pixels per reach-granule: (a) it is density-weighted (the 3,735 px at Uyak node 35 vs ~200 px/node upstream on 2023-09-01 pull the fit toward the downstream reach — the exact bias the node-binned Theil-Sen reference gradient was introduced to fix), and (b) it is computed on whatever survives the upstream defects: on the 50 pass-571 dates it is a 'reach gradient' fit over only km 30.7-35.1, and on the 46 MAD-amputated Uyak dates over the truncated lower profile. These values are stored in every daily CSV, kept by KEEP_COLUMNS into the master parquet, and shipped to the dashboard, where they are indistinguishable from full-reach gradients.
failure_scenario: For 2023-11-03 Uyak, slope_calc in the master is an OLS over km 20-36 only (upstream amputated); for any pass-571 date it is an OLS over km 30.7-35.1 of Kanektok. A dashboard user or script averaging slope_calc across passes mixes full-reach and 5-km-stub 'gradients' with no flag distinguishing them.
suggested_fix: Either drop slope_calc from the export (the reference-gradient artifact is the authoritative slope) or store it alongside lo_km/hi_km/n so consumers can gate on coverage, mirroring the refgrad gate.

title: Unparseable granule names collapse onto one 'Unknown_Date' CSV and would crash compute_reference_gradient
description: If the timestamp regex walk fails (line 204-216), formatted_date becomes 'Unknown_Date': every such granule writes/overwrites the single file Unknown_Date_data.csv (line 352), and extract_date_from_granule returns None so the skip check never blocks reprocessing. At rebuild, rows with Pass_Date='Unknown_Date' pass the KNOWN_BAD filter and column pruning, then `pd.to_datetime(df['Pass_Date'])` at line 410 raises on the unparseable string, aborting the reference-gradient step after the master files are already written (master and refgrad artifacts go out of sync). Not currently triggered (all 189 CSVs are date-named), but a PGE naming change or a differently-formatted collection would hit it.
failure_scenario: A granule named without a 15-char YYYYMMDDTHHMMSS token is processed -> Unknown_Date_data.csv written -> next rebuild: master parquet includes Pass_Date='Unknown_Date' rows, then compute_reference_gradient raises ValueError/DateParseError at pd.to_datetime, so reference_gradient_per_pass.parquet is left stale relative to the new master.
suggested_fix: Treat an unparseable date as a hard skip (log and continue) instead of processing under a sentinel name; or validate Pass_Date with `pd.to_datetime(..., errors='coerce')` and drop/report NaT rows at rebuild.

title: Failed and empty downloads vanish without accounting; failures re-attempted every run with no record
description: `if not files: return None` (line 220) drops a granule with no message at all; the catch-all except (line 359) reduces any error (network, NetCDF corruption, the astype crash above) to one scrolling tqdm line. main() tracks processed_count and skipped_count but no failed_count, and the summary (line 596) plus the immediately-following master rebuild give no signal that granules are missing. Granules that legitimately yield no polygon data also never write a checkpoint, so they are re-downloaded on every single resume run (53 pass-265 granules and ~10 others, i.e. ~60+ full PIXC downloads repeated per run).
failure_scenario: A transient Earthdata outage during a 400-granule run fails 30 downloads; the run ends with '📊 Summary: 340 new, 30 skipped'-style output that never mentions the 30 failures, and the master is rebuilt and published incomplete. Verified the no-yield case from CMR-vs-disk: the 53 pass-265 dates have no CSVs, so every resume re-downloads all 53.
suggested_fix: Count and print failures in the summary (and exit nonzero or warn before rebuilding if any); write a zero-byte or sentinel checkpoint (e.g., `{date}_empty.marker`) for granules that legitimately produce no polygon data.

title: Polygon file with missing CRS is silently assumed EPSG:4326
description: `if gdf.crs and gdf.crs.to_string() != 'EPSG:4326'` reprojects only when a CRS is present; a shapefile missing its .prj loads with crs=None and is used as-is with no warning. If the polygons were in a projected CRS (e.g., the ArcticDEM work uses polar stereographic), coordinates in meters would never intersect the lon/lat pixel cloud and every granule would 'process' to zero points — a silent all-data-lost mode rather than an error. The current river_poly.zip is verified fine (EPSG:4326, fields id/Name resolve via the id path in resolve_poly_name), so this is latent.
failure_scenario: User regenerates river_poly.zip from a GIS export that drops the .prj (crs=None) while the geometry is in EPSG:3413 meters: load_polygons prints '✅ Loaded 2 polygons', every granule returns None (no rough-bbox matches), and the run completes 'successfully' having ingested nothing.
suggested_fix: Fail hard when gdf.crs is None (or set_crs with an explicit, logged assumption), and sanity-check total_bounds against valid lon/lat ranges before searching.
